sentences.zh: 【晉紀十六】　起著雍困敦，盡重光單閼，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 16] From the year wuzi (Zhuyong/Kundun) through xinchou (Chongguang/Shanyan), four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Records 16] Spanning the years 328–331 CE (from wuzi through xinchou in the sexagenary cycle), four years in all.

sentences.zh: 顯宗成皇帝上之下咸和三年（

translations.literal: Lower fascicle of the reign of Emperor Cheng the Manifest Ancestor, Xianhe year 3 (
translations.idiomatic: From the lower fascicle of the reign of Emperor Cheng (Manifest Ancestor), Xianhe year 3 (

sentences.zh: 戊子，公元三二八年）

translations.literal: wuzi, corresponding to 328 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuzi, corresponding to 328 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，溫嶠入救建康，軍於尋陽。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Wen Jiao marched to relieve Jiankang and encamped at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Wen Jiao set out to relieve Jiankang and halted his army at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 韓晃襲司馬流於慈湖；

translations.literal: Han Huang attacked Sima Liu at Cihu;
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang attacked Sima Liu at Cihu;

sentences.zh: 流素懦怯，將戰，食炙不知口處，兵敗而死。

translations.literal: Liu had always been timid and cowardly; on the eve of battle, while eating roast meat he could not find his mouth with the food, and after his army was defeated he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu had always been timid; on the eve of battle, while eating roast meat he could not even find his mouth, and after his army was routed he was killed.

sentences.zh: 丁未，蘇峻帥祖渙、許柳等眾二萬人，濟自橫江，登牛渚，軍於陵口。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, Su Jun led Zu Huan, Xu Liu, and others with a host of twenty thousand men, crossed from Hengjiang, ascended Niuzhu, and encamped at Lingkou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Su Jun led Zu Huan, Xu Liu, and the rest with twenty thousand troops, crossed at Hengjiang, took Niuzhu, and encamped at Lingkou.

sentences.zh: 台兵御之，屢敗。

translations.literal: The capital troops opposed them and were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The capital forces met them and were beaten again and again.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚戌，峻至蔣陵覆舟山。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day gengxu, Jun reached Jiangling at Fuzhoushan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengxu, Jun reached Jiangling at Mount Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 陶回謂庾亮曰：「峻知石頭有重戍，不敢直下，必向小丹楊南道步來；

translations.literal: Tao Hui said to Yu Liang: "Jun knows that Shitou has heavy garrisons and will not dare come straight down; he is sure to come by foot along the southern road through Lesser Danyang;
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hui told Yu Liang, "Jun knows Shitou is heavily garrisoned and will not dare come straight in; he is sure to march along the southern road through Lesser Danyang;

sentences.zh: 宜伏兵邀之，可一戰擒也。

translations.literal: we ought to set an ambush to intercept him, and he can be captured in a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: we should lay an ambush and take him in one fight."

sentences.zh: 」亮不從。

translations.literal: " Liang did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 峻果自小丹楊來，迷失道，夜行，無復部分。

translations.literal: Jun did indeed come by way of Lesser Danyang, lost his way, marched by night, and his forces lost all formation.
translations.idiomatic: Jun did come by Lesser Danyang, lost the road, marched at night, and his army fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 亮聞，乃悔之。

translations.literal: When Liang heard of it, he regretted his decision.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang heard this, he regretted not having listened.

sentences.zh: 朝士以京邑危逼，多遣家人入東避難，左衛將軍劉超獨遷妻孥入居宮內。

translations.literal: Because the capital was in peril, many court officials sent their families east to escape; only the Left Guard General Liu Chao moved his wife and children into the palace to live.
translations.idiomatic: With the capital under threat, many officials sent their families east to safety; only Left Guard General Liu Chao brought his wife and children into the palace.

sentences.zh: 詔以卞壼都督大桁東諸軍事，與侍中鐘雅帥郭默、趙胤等軍及峻戰於西陵。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Bian Kun commander of all forces east of the Great Pontoon Bridge, and with Palace Attendant Zhong Ya he led the armies of Guo Mo, Zhao Yin, and others to give battle to Jun at Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Kun was ordered to command all forces east of the Great Pontoon Bridge; with Palace Attendant Zhong Ya he led Guo Mo, Zhao Yin, and the rest against Jun at Xiling.

sentences.zh: 壼等大敗，死傷以千數。

translations.literal: Kun and the others were utterly defeated; dead and wounded numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Kun's force was routed, with thousands killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，峻攻青溪柵，卞壼帥諸軍拒擊，不能禁。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Jun attacked the Qingxi stockade; Bian Kun led the various armies to resist but could not hold him back.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Jun assaulted the Qingxi stockade; Bian Kun led the armies in defense but could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 峻因風縱火，燒台省及諸營寺署，一時蕩盡。

translations.literal: Jun took advantage of the wind to set fires that burned the central administration and all barracks, monasteries, and offices, sweeping them away at once.
translations.idiomatic: Jun used the wind to set fires that consumed the central offices and every camp, monastery, and bureau in one sweep.

sentences.zh: 壼背癰新愈，創猶未合，力疾帥左右苦戰而死；

translations.literal: Kun's back carbuncle had only just healed and the wound was not yet closed; forcing himself despite illness, he led his close attendants in bitter fighting and died;
translations.idiomatic: Kun's back abscess had only just healed and the wound was still open; straining himself despite his illness, he led his personal guard in fierce fighting until he fell;

sentences.zh: 二子□□、盱隨父後，亦赴敵而死。

translations.literal: his two sons [Zhun] and Xu followed close behind their father and likewise went to meet the enemy and died.
translations.idiomatic: his two sons Zhun and Xu followed their father into the fight and were also killed.

sentences.zh: 其母撫屍哭曰：「父為忠臣，子為孝子，夫何恨乎！

translations.literal: Their mother stroked the corpses and wept, saying, "The father was a loyal minister and the sons filial sons—what is there to regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Their mother embraced the bodies and wept: "A loyal father and filial sons—what more could one ask?"

sentences.zh: 」丹楊尹羊曼勒兵守雲龍門，與黃門侍郎周導、廬江太守陶瞻皆戰死。

translations.literal: " The Danyang intendant Yang Man mustered troops to hold the Cloud Dragon Gate; he, Yellow Gate Attendant Zhou Dao, and Lujiang grand administrator Tao Zhan all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: " Danyang intendant Yang Man held the Cloud Dragon Gate with his troops; Yellow Gate Attendant Zhou Dao and Lujiang administrator Tao Zhan all fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 庾亮帥眾將陳於宣陽門內，未及成列，士眾皆棄甲走，亮與弟懌、條、翼及郭默、趙胤俱奔尋陽。

translations.literal: Yu Liang led his generals to form ranks inside the Xuanyang Gate; before the lines were complete the soldiers all cast off their armor and fled. Liang, his brothers Yi, Tiao, and Yi, and Guo Mo and Zhao Yin all fled to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang drew up his generals inside the Xuanyang Gate, but before the ranks were formed the troops threw off their armor and ran. Liang fled to Xunyang with his brothers Yi, Tiao, and Yi and with Guo Mo and Zhao Yin.

sentences.zh: 將行，顧謂鐘雅曰：「後事深以相委。

translations.literal: As he was about to leave, he turned and said to Zhong Ya, "I entrust what comes after to you in full."
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving, he turned to Zhong Ya and said, "I leave what follows entirely in your hands."

sentences.zh: 」雅曰：「棟折榱崩，誰之咎也！

translations.literal: " Ya said, "When the ridgepole breaks and the rafters collapse, whose fault is it!"
translations.idiomatic: " Ya replied, "When the ridgepole snaps and the rafters fall, whose fault is that?"

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「今日之事，不容復言。

translations.literal: " Liang said, "Today's affair brooks no further words."
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said, "There is nothing more to say about today."

sentences.zh: 」亮乘小船，亂兵相剝掠；

translations.literal: " Liang boarded a small boat; disorderly soldiers plundered one another;
translations.idiomatic: " Liang took a small boat; in the chaos soldiers robbed one another;

sentences.zh: 亮左右射賊，誤中柁工，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Liang's attendants shot at bandits and by mistake struck the helmsman, who fell at the twang of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: his men shot at marauders and accidentally hit the helmsman, who dropped at once.

sentences.zh: 船上咸失色慾散，亮不動，徐曰：「此手何可使著賊！

translations.literal: Everyone on the boat turned pale and wanted to scatter; Liang did not stir and said calmly, "How could this hand be allowed to strike our own men!"
translations.idiomatic: Everyone on board turned pale and nearly panicked; Liang did not move and said calmly, "How could we let our arrows strike our own people!"

sentences.zh: 」眾乃安。

translations.literal: " Only then did the company settle.
translations.idiomatic: " The men then calmed down.

sentences.zh: 峻兵入台城，司徒導謂侍中褚翜曰：「至尊當御正殿，君可啟令速出。

translations.literal: Jun's troops entered the Terrace City. Grand Mentor Dao said to Palace Attendant Chu Pou: "His Majesty should attend the main hall; you may announce and have him come out at once."
translations.idiomatic: When Jun's troops entered the Terrace City, Grand Mentor Wang Dao told Palace Attendant Chu Pou, "His Majesty should take the main throne hall—please announce and bring him out at once."

sentences.zh: 」翜即入上閤，躬自抱帝登太極前殿；

translations.literal: " Pou at once entered the upper pavilion, personally carried the emperor in his arms up to the front hall of the Hall of Supreme Pole;
translations.idiomatic: " Pou went straight to the upper pavilion, lifted the emperor in his arms, and carried him to the front hall of the Hall of Supreme Pole;

sentences.zh: 導及光祿大夫陸曄、荀崧、尚書張闓共登御床，擁衛帝。

translations.literal: Dao and Household Counsellor Lu Ye, Xun Song, and Secretary Zhang Kai all mounted the imperial couch to shield and guard the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Dao, Household Counsellor Lu Ye, Xun Song, and Secretary Zhang Kai climbed onto the imperial couch to shield the emperor.

sentences.zh: 以劉超為右衛將軍，使與鐘雅、褚翜侍立左右，太常孔愉朝服守宗廟。

translations.literal: Liu Chao was made Right Guard General and ordered to stand in attendance with Zhong Ya and Chu Pou at left and right; the Minister of Ceremonies Kong Yu in court dress guarded the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chao was appointed Right Guard General to stand with Zhong Ya and Chu Pou at the emperor's side, while Minister of Ceremonies Kong Yu in full court dress guarded the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 時百官奔散，殿省蕭然。

translations.literal: At the time the hundred officials had fled in disorder, and the halls and offices were desolate.
translations.idiomatic: By then the officials had scattered, and the palace halls stood empty.

sentences.zh: 峻兵既入，叱褚翜令下翜正立不動，呵之曰：「蘇冠軍來覲至尊，軍人豈得侵逼！

translations.literal: Once Jun's soldiers had entered, they shouted at Chu Pou to step down; Pou stood upright and did not move, rebuking them: "General Su Champion has come to attend upon His Majesty—how dare soldiers press upon him!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jun's troops entered, they ordered Chu Pou down; Pou stood firm and rebuked them: "Champion-General Su has come to pay his respects to His Majesty—soldiers must not crowd the throne!"

sentences.zh: 」由是峻兵不敢上殿，突入後宮，宮人及太后左右侍人皆見掠奪。

translations.literal: " Because of this Jun's troops did not dare ascend the hall; they burst into the inner palace, and palace women and the attendants at the empress dowager's side were all plundered.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun's men dared not enter the hall; they stormed the inner palace instead, and palace women and the empress dowager's attendants were looted.

sentences.zh: 峻兵驅役百官，光祿勳王彬等皆被捶撻，令負提登蔣山。

translations.literal: Jun's troops drove the hundred officials as laborers; Household Excellency Wang Bin and others were all beaten and made to carry loads up Mount Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's men pressed the officials into labor; Household Excellency Wang Bin and others were beaten and forced to haul burdens up Mount Jiang.

sentences.zh: 裸剝士女，皆以壞席苦苫草自鄣，無草者坐地以土自覆；

translations.literal: Men and women were stripped naked; all used ruined mats and coarse rush grass to cover themselves, and those without grass sat on the ground and covered themselves with earth;
translations.idiomatic: Men and women were stripped; they shielded themselves with torn mats and coarse rush, and those without even rush sat on the ground and covered themselves with dirt;

sentences.zh: 哀號之聲，震動內外。

translations.literal: the sound of wailing shook inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: their cries of anguish shook the city inside and out.

sentences.zh: 初，姑孰既陷，尚書左丞孔坦謂人曰：「觀峻之勢，必破台城，自非戰士，不須戎服。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Gushu had fallen, Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing Kong Tan said to others: "Judging by Jun's momentum, he is sure to breach the Terrace City; unless one is a fighting man, there is no need for military dress."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Gushu fell, Left Assistant Kong Tan had told people, "Jun's momentum means the Terrace City will fall—unless you are a soldier, do not wear armor."

sentences.zh: 」及台城陷，戎服者多死，白衣者無他。

translations.literal: " When the Terrace City fell, many in military dress died, while those in plain clothes suffered no special harm.
translations.idiomatic: " When the city fell, many in armor died, while those in civilian dress were spared.

sentences.zh: 時官有布二十萬匹，金銀五千斤，錢億萬，絹數萬匹，他物稱是，峻盡費之；

translations.literal: At the time the government had two hundred thousand bolts of cloth, five thousand jin of gold and silver, a hundred million in cash, and tens of thousands of bolts of silk, with other goods in proportion; Jun spent them all;
translations.idiomatic: The treasury held two hundred thousand bolts of cloth, five thousand jin of gold and silver, a hundred million cash, and tens of thousands of bolts of silk, with other stores to match; Jun squandered it all;

sentences.zh: 太官惟有燒餘米數石以供御膳。

translations.literal: the Imperial Kitchen had only a few piculs of rice left from the fire to supply the imperial meals.
translations.idiomatic: the Imperial Kitchen had only a few piculs of fire-scorched rice left for the emperor's table.

sentences.zh: 或謂鐘雅曰：「君性亮直，必不容於寇仇，盍早為之計！

translations.literal: Someone said to Zhong Ya: "Your nature is bright and upright; the rebel enemy will surely not tolerate you—why not plan early!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Zhong Ya, "You are forthright by nature; the rebels will never spare you—why not act while you can?"

sentences.zh: 」雅曰：「國亂不能匡，君危不能濟，各遁逃以求免，何以為臣！

translations.literal: " Ya said, "When the state is in turmoil one cannot set it right, when the ruler is in peril one cannot rescue him—if each flees to save himself, how can one be called a minister!"
translations.idiomatic: " Ya replied, "When the realm is in chaos and the ruler in peril, if every man flees to save himself, what sort of minister is that?"

sentences.zh: 丁巳，峻稱詔大赦，惟庾亮兄弟不在原例。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, Jun proclaimed an edict of general amnesty, except that the brothers Yu Liang were not within the scope of pardon.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Jun proclaimed a general amnesty by imperial edict, excluding the Yu Liang brothers.

sentences.zh: 以王導有德望，猶使以本官居己之右。

translations.literal: Because Wang Dao had moral stature and renown, Jun still had him keep his original office and sit to Jun's right.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Wang Dao's prestige, Jun let him keep his rank and seat him to his own right.

sentences.zh: 祖約為侍中、太尉、尚書令，峻自為驃騎將軍、錄尚書事，許柳為丹楊尹，馬雄為左衛將軍，祖渙為驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Zu Yue was made Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, and Director of the Masters of Writing; Jun made himself General of Agile Cavalry and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; Xu Liu was Danyang intendant, Ma Xiong Left Guard General, and Zu Huan General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue became Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, and Director of the Masters of Writing; Jun took for himself General of Agile Cavalry and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; Xu Liu became Danyang intendant, Ma Xiong Left Guard General, and Zu Huan General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 弋陽王羕詣峻，稱述峻功，峻復以羕為西陽王、太宰、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yiyang, Sima Yi, went to Jun and extolled Jun's achievements; Jun in turn made Yi Prince of Xiyang, Grand Tutor, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yiyang Sima Yi came to Jun and praised his exploits; Jun in return made him Prince of Xiyang, Grand Tutor, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 峻遣兵攻吳國內史庾冰，冰不能御，棄郡奔會稽，至浙江，峻購之甚急。

translations.literal: Jun sent troops to attack Wu interior administrator Yu Bing; Bing could not resist, abandoned the commandery and fled to Kuaiji, and when he reached the Zhe River Jun offered a rich reward for his capture.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent troops against Wu interior administrator Yu Bing; Bing could not hold the commandery, fled toward Kuaiji, and by the time he reached the Zhe River Jun had posted a heavy price on his head.

sentences.zh: 吳鈴下卒引冰入船，以蘧蒢覆之，呤嘯鼓枻，溯流而去。

translations.literal: A Wu runner under the commandery led Bing into a boat, covered him with coarse rush matting, hummed and whistled while beating the oar, and went upstream.
translations.idiomatic: A Wu commandery runner took Bing aboard, covered him with rush matting, and rowed upstream humming and whistling as though drunk.

sentences.zh: 每逢邏所，輒以杖叩船曰：「何處覓庾冰，庚冰正在此。

translations.literal: Whenever they met a patrol post he would tap the boat with his staff and say, "Where can one find Yu Bing? Geng Bing is right here."
translations.idiomatic: At every patrol station he would rap the boat with his staff and shout, "Where's Yu Bing? Geng Bing's right here!"

sentences.zh: 」人以為醉，不疑之，冰僅免。

translations.literal: " People thought him drunk and did not suspect; Bing barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: " They took him for a drunk and never searched the boat; Bing barely got away.

sentences.zh: 峻以侍中蔡謨為吳國內史。

translations.literal: Jun appointed Palace Attendant Cai Mo Wu interior administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made Palace Attendant Cai Mo the new Wu interior administrator.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠聞建康不守，號慟；

translations.literal: When Wen Jiao heard that Jiankang could not be held, he wailed in grief;
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Jiao learned that Jiankang had fallen, he broke into loud mourning;

sentences.zh: 人有候之者，悲哭相對。

translations.literal: when anyone came to visit him, they wept together in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: and anyone who came to see him joined in weeping face to face.

sentences.zh: 庾亮至尋陽，宣太后詔，以嶠為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，又加徐州刺史郗鑒司空。

translations.literal: When Yu Liang reached Xunyang he proclaimed the empress dowager's edict, making Jiao General of Agile Cavalry with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and further promoting Xu Province inspector Xi Jian to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Liang reached Xunyang he announced the empress dowager's edict appointing Jiao General of Agile Cavalry with privilege of an independent staff, and promoting Xu Province inspector Xi Jian to Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「今日當以滅賊為急，未有功而先拜官，將何以示天下！

translations.literal: Jiao said, "Today we must make destroying the rebels our urgent task; to accept office before any achievement—how would that look to the empire!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiao said, "Our urgent task is to destroy the rebels—how can we accept promotion before we have won? What would the empire think?"

sentences.zh: 」遂不受。

translations.literal: " He therefore did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " He declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 嶠素重亮，亮雖奔敗，嶠愈推奉之，分兵給亮。

translations.literal: Jiao had always esteemed Liang; though Liang had fled in defeat, Jiao honored him all the more and divided troops to give him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao had always respected Liang; despite Liang's rout, Jiao treated him with even greater deference and gave him a share of the army.

sentences.zh: 後趙大赦，改元太和。

translations.literal: Later Zhao proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao declared a general amnesty and adopted the era name Taihe.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙子，庾太后以憂崩。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day bingzi, Empress Dowager Yu died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingzi, Empress Dowager Yu died of grief.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻南屯於湖。

translations.literal: Su Jun encamped south at Yuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun moved south and encamped at Yuhu.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，後趙將石堪攻宛，南陽太守王國降之；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Later Zhao general Shi Kan attacked Wan, and Nanyang grand administrator Wang Guo surrendered to him;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Later Zhao general Shi Kan attacked Wan, and Nanyang administrator Wang Guo surrendered;

sentences.zh: 遂進攻祖約軍於淮上。

translations.literal: he then advanced to attack Zu Yue's army on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: then pressed on to attack Zu Yue's army on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 約將陳光起兵攻約，約左右閻禿，貌類約，光謂為約而擒之。

translations.literal: Yue's general Chen Guang raised troops to attack Yue; Yue's attendant Yan Tu resembled Yue in appearance, and Guang thought him to be Yue and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's general Chen Guang rose against him; Yan Tu, a man at Yue's side who looked like him, was mistaken for Yue and captured.

sentences.zh: 約逾垣獲免，光奔後趙。

translations.literal: Yue climbed over a wall and escaped; Guang fled to Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yue climbed a wall and escaped; Guang fled to Later Zhao.

sentences.zh: 壬申，葬明穆皇后於武平陵。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Empress Mingmu was buried at Wuping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Empress Mingmu was interred at Wuping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 庾亮、溫嶠將起兵討蘇峻，而道路斷絕，不知建康聲聞。

translations.literal: Yu Liang and Wen Jiao were about to raise troops to punish Su Jun, but communications were cut and they had no news from Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang and Wen Jiao were preparing to march against Su Jun, but the roads were cut and they had no word from Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 會南陽范汪至尋陽，言「峻政令不壹，貪暴縱橫，滅亡已兆，雖強易弱，朝廷有倒懸之急，宜時進討。

translations.literal: It happened that Fan Wang of Nanyang reached Xunyang and said, "Jun's orders are inconsistent, he is greedy and violent without restraint, and the signs of ruin are already plain; though he seems strong he is easy to overcome. The court hangs upside down in peril and should advance to attack at once."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wang of Nanyang arrived at Xunyang and said, "Jun's rule is chaotic and his greed and violence unrestrained—the omens of collapse are already clear. Though he seems strong he is easily beaten. The court is in desperate peril; you should attack now."

sentences.zh: 」嶠深納之。

translations.literal: " Jiao took this deeply to heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiao took his advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 亮辟汪參護軍事。

translations.literal: Liang recruited Wang as a staff officer on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liang appointed Wang to his military staff.

sentences.zh: 亮、嶠互相推為盟主，嶠從弟充曰：「陶征西位重兵強，宜共推之。

translations.literal: Liang and Jiao each urged the other to be alliance leader; Jiao's cousin Chong said, "Western Campaigning General Tao holds high rank and strong forces—we ought jointly to push him forward."
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Jiao each declined leadership in favor of the other; Jiao's cousin Wen Chong said, "General Tao the Western Campaigner outranks us and commands the strongest army—we should make him our leader."

sentences.zh: 」嶠乃遣督護王愆期詣荊州，邀陶侃與之同赴國難。

translations.literal: " Jiao then sent Supervisor Wang Yanqi to Jing Province to invite Tao Kan to share in meeting the state's crisis.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiao sent Supervisor Wang Yanqi to Jing Province to invite Tao Kan to join them in saving the realm.

sentences.zh: 侃猶以不豫顧命為恨，答曰：「吾疆場外將，不敢越局。

translations.literal: Kan still harbored resentment that he had not been included in the deathbed testament, and replied, "I am a frontier general outside the capital—I dare not overstep my charge."
translations.idiomatic: Kan still resented being left out of the deathbed regency, and replied, "I am a frontier commander—I dare not overstep my post."

sentences.zh: 」嶠屢說，不能回；

translations.literal: " Jiao urged him repeatedly but could not turn him;
translations.idiomatic: " Jiao pleaded repeatedly but could not move him;

sentences.zh: 乃順侃意，遣使謂之曰：「仁公且守，僕當先下。

translations.literal: he then yielded to Kan's wish and sent a messenger saying, "My lord, hold your position; I shall go down first."
translations.idiomatic: so he yielded and sent word: "My lord, hold your ground; I will march first."

sentences.zh: 」使者去已二日，平南參軍滎陽毛寶別使還，聞之，說嶠曰：「凡舉大事，當與天下共之。

translations.literal: " The messenger had been gone two days when Pingnan staff officer Mao Bao of Xingyang, returning from a separate mission, heard of it and said to Jiao, "Whenever one undertakes a great affair, one should share it with the empire."
translations.idiomatic: " Two days after the messenger left, staff officer Mao Bao of Xingyang returned from another errand, heard what had been sent, and told Jiao, "Any great undertaking must be shared with all under heaven."

sentences.zh: 師克在和，不宜異同。

translations.literal: Armies conquer through harmony; one should not foster division.
translations.idiomatic: Victory depends on unity; you must not sow discord.

sentences.zh: 假令可疑，猶當外示不覺，況自為攜貳邪！

translations.literal: Even if there were grounds for suspicion, one should still outwardly show no awareness—how much less deliberately create a split!
translations.idiomatic: Even if he were suspect, you should show no sign of it—how much less deliberately divide the alliance!

sentences.zh: 宜急追信改書，言必應俱進；

translations.literal: You ought urgently to overtake the messenger and change the letter, saying you will surely advance together;
translations.idiomatic: You must overtake that messenger and change the letter to say you will advance together;

sentences.zh: 若不及前信，當更遣使。

translations.literal: if you cannot catch the earlier message, you should send another envoy.
translations.idiomatic: if you cannot catch him, send another envoy at once.

sentences.zh: 」嶠意悟，即追使者，改書；

translations.literal: " Jiao understood, at once overtook the messenger and altered the letter;
translations.idiomatic: " Jiao saw the point, overtook the messenger, and rewrote the letter;

sentences.zh: 侃果許之，遣督護龔登帥兵詣嶠。

translations.literal: Kan indeed agreed and sent Supervisor Gong Deng to lead troops to Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Kan agreed and sent Supervisor Gong Deng with troops to join Jiao.

sentences.zh: 嶠有眾七千，於是列上尚書，陳祖約、蘇峻罪狀，移告征鎮，灑泣登舟。

translations.literal: Jiao had seven thousand men; he then submitted a memorial to the Masters of Writing setting forth the crimes of Zu Yue and Su Jun, circulated proclamations to the campaigning generals and regional commanders, and boarded his ships in tears.
translations.idiomatic: With seven thousand men, Jiao memorialized the Masters of Writing listing the crimes of Zu Yue and Su Jun, sent proclamations to the regional commanders, and boarded his fleet in tears.

sentences.zh: 陶侃復追龔登還。

translations.literal: Tao Kan again recalled Gong Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan then recalled Gong Deng.

sentences.zh: 嶠遺侃書曰：「夫軍有進而無退，可增而不可減。

translations.literal: Jiao sent Kan a letter saying, "In military affairs there is advance but no retreat; forces may be increased but not reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Jiao wrote to Kan: "An army may advance but never retreat; it may grow but never shrink."

sentences.zh: 近已移檄遠近，言於盟府，刻後月半大舉，諸郡軍並在路次，惟須仁公軍至，便齊進耳。

translations.literal: I have lately sent proclamations far and near, informing the alliance headquarters that a major campaign is set for the middle of next month; the armies of the various commanderies are all on the march, and only await my lord's forces to arrive for a joint advance."
translations.idiomatic: I have already proclaimed to the alliance that we strike in mid-month; every commandery army is on the road, waiting only for your troops to march together."

sentences.zh: 仁公今召軍還，疑惑遠近，成敗之由，將在於此。

translations.literal: My lord now recalls your army—this will breed doubt near and far, and victory or defeat may hinge upon it.
translations.idiomatic: If you recall your army now, you will sow doubt everywhere, and success or failure may turn on this alone.

sentences.zh: 僕才輕任重，實憑仁公篤愛，遠稟成規；

translations.literal: My talent is slight for the burden I bear; I truly rely on my lord's steadfast regard and take my plans from afar under your guidance;
translations.idiomatic: My abilities are slight for so heavy a charge; I rely on your steadfast support and take my guidance from you;

sentences.zh: 至於首啟戎行，不敢有辭，僕與仁公，如首尾相衛，脣齒相依也。

translations.literal: as for being first to open the campaign, I dare make no complaint—you and I, my lord, are like head and tail guarding each other, lips and teeth depending on one another.
translations.idiomatic: as for leading the march, I make no complaint—you and I, my lord, are head and tail, lips and teeth.

sentences.zh: 恐或者不達高旨，將謂仁公緩於討賊，此聲難追。

translations.literal: I fear some may not grasp your lofty intent and will say my lord is slow to punish the rebels—a reputation hard to retrieve.
translations.idiomatic: I fear some will not understand your intent and will say you are slow to punish the rebels—a rumor once spread is hard to recall.

sentences.zh: 僕與仁公並受方岳之任，安危休戚，理既同之。

translations.literal: You and I alike bear the charge of a regional pillar; in safety and peril, weal and woe, our lot is by right the same.
translations.idiomatic: We both hold regional command; in safety and danger, weal and woe, our fates are bound together.

sentences.zh: 且自頃之顧，綢繆往來，情深義重，一旦有急，亦望仁公悉眾見救，況社稷之難乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, since our recent mutual regard and close exchanges, our bond has been deep in feeling and weighty in obligation—if an emergency arose I would still hope my lord would bring all your forces to the rescue; how much more in the realm's crisis!
translations.idiomatic: Our recent friendship has been close and our obligations weighty—if trouble came I would still expect you to march to my aid with all your forces; how much more now, when the altars of state are at stake!

sentences.zh: 今日之憂，豈惟僕一州，文武莫不翹企。

translations.literal: Today's anxiety is not mine alone in one province—all civil and military officials crane their necks in expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Today's crisis is not mine alone—every official in the empire watches and waits.

sentences.zh: 假令此州不守，約、峻樹置官長於此，荊楚西逼強胡，東接逆賊，因之以饑饉，將來之危，乃當甚於此州之今日也。

translations.literal: If this province cannot be held and Yue and Jun establish officials here, Jing and Chu will press against the fierce barbarians in the west and border the rebel enemy in the east; with famine added, the peril to come will be even greater than this province's plight today.
translations.idiomatic: If we lose this province and Yue and Jun set up their officials here, Jing and Chu will be squeezed between the barbarians in the west and the rebels in the east; with famine on top of that, the danger ahead will exceed what we face today.

sentences.zh: 仁公進當為大晉之忠臣，參桓、文之功；

translations.literal: If my lord advances, you should be a loyal minister of Great Jin, sharing in the achievements of Duke Huan and Duke Wen;
translations.idiomatic: If you advance, you will be a loyal minister of Jin, ranking with Duke Huan and Duke Wen of old;

sentences.zh: 退當以慈父之情，雪愛子之痛。

translations.literal: if you retreat, you should in a father's tender feeling wipe away a beloved son's pain.
translations.idiomatic: if you hold back, you can as a grieving father avenge a beloved son's death.

sentences.zh: 今約、峻凶逆無道，痛感天地，人心齊壹，咸皆切齒。

translations.literal: Now Yue and Jun are vicious rebels without the Way, their cruelty moving heaven and earth; hearts are united, and all grind their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Yue and Jun are monstrous rebels whose crimes shock heaven and earth; all men are of one mind and grind their teeth in rage.

sentences.zh: 今之進討，若以石投卵耳；

translations.literal: Today's advance to punish them is like casting a stone at an egg;
translations.idiomatic: To march against them now is like throwing a stone at an egg;

sentences.zh: 苟復召兵還，是為敗於幾成也。

translations.literal: if you again recall your troops, you will have failed on the verge of success.
translations.idiomatic: if you recall your army again, you will snatch defeat from the brink of victory.

sentences.zh: 願深察所陳！

translations.literal: I beg you to examine deeply what I have set forth!
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to weigh these words carefully!

sentences.zh: 」王愆期謂侃曰：「蘇峻，豺狼也，如得遂志，四海雖廣，公寧有容足之地乎！

translations.literal: " Wang Yanqi said to Kan: "Su Jun is a wolf; if he fulfills his aims, though the four seas are vast, will you, sir, have a place to set your foot!"
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Yanqi told Kan, "Su Jun is a wolf. If he gets his way, will you have room to stand anywhere under heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」侃深感悟，即戎服登舟；

translations.literal: " Kan was deeply moved to understanding, at once donned armor and boarded his ship;
translations.idiomatic: " Deeply moved, Kan put on armor and boarded his ship at once;

sentences.zh: 瞻喪至不臨，晝夜兼道而進。

translations.literal: when Zhan's funeral arrived he did not attend but pressed on day and night by double marches.
translations.idiomatic: he did not pause even when Tao Zhan's funeral arrived, but marched day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 郗鑒在廣陵，城孤糧少，逼近胡寇，人無固志。

translations.literal: Xi Jian was at Guangling; the city was isolated and grain scant, the barbarian enemy pressed close, and men had no firm will.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian held Guangling, where the city was isolated, provisions were low, barbarian raiders pressed near, and morale was uncertain.

sentences.zh: 得詔書，即流涕誓眾，入赴國難，將士爭奮。

translations.literal: On receiving the imperial edict he at once wept, swore the host to the oath, and marched to meet the state's crisis; officers and soldiers vied in ardor.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived he wept before his troops, swore them to the cause, and marched to save the realm; officers and men vied to follow.

sentences.zh: 遣將軍夏侯長等間行謂溫嶠曰：「或聞賊欲挾天子東入會稽，當先立營壘，屯據要害，既防其越逸，又斷賊糧運，然後清野堅壁以待賊。

translations.literal: He sent Generals Xiahou Chang and others by secret route to tell Wen Jiao: "It is heard that the rebels wish to take the Son of Heaven east into Kuaiji; we should first raise ramparts and camp at strategic points, both to prevent their escape and to cut the rebels' grain transport, then clear the countryside and hold fast in our walls to await the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Xiahou Chang and others by secret route to Wen Jiao: "Some say the rebels mean to take the emperor east to Kuaiji. We should first build camps at key points to block their escape and cut their supply lines, then strip the countryside and hold our walls until they come."

sentences.zh: 賊攻城不拔，野無所掠，東道既斷，糧運自絕，必自潰矣。

translations.literal: The rebels will fail to take the city by assault; with nothing to plunder in the fields, the eastern route cut, and grain transport ended, they are sure to collapse of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They will fail to take our cities, find nothing to loot in the fields, and with the eastern route cut and supplies gone, they will collapse on their own.

sentences.zh: 」嶠深以為然。

translations.literal: " Jiao deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiao agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 五月，陶侃帥眾至尋陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Tao Kan led his host to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Tao Kan brought his army to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 議者咸謂侃欲誅庾亮以謝天下；

translations.literal: Those in council all said Kan wished to execute Yu Liang to appease the empire;
translations.idiomatic: Many believed Kan intended to execute Yu Liang to satisfy the realm;

sentences.zh: 亮甚懼，用溫嶠計，詣侃拜謝。

translations.literal: Liang was greatly afraid and, using Wen Jiao's plan, went to Kan to bow in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was terrified and, on Wen Jiao's advice, went to Kan to apologize in person.

sentences.zh: 侃驚，止之曰：「庾元規乃拜陶士行邪！

translations.literal: Kan was startled and stopped him, saying, "Yu Yuangui bowing to Tao Shixing!"
translations.idiomatic: Kan was astonished and stopped him: "Yu Yuangui bowing to Tao Shixing!"

sentences.zh: 」亮引咎自責，風止可觀，侃不覺釋然，曰：「君侯修石頭以擬老子，今日反見求邪！

translations.literal: " Liang took blame upon himself; his bearing was admirable to behold, and Kan unawares relaxed and said, "My lord, you fortified Shitou to match this old man—today you come seeking me instead!"
translations.idiomatic: " Liang took all blame on himself with such dignity that Kan's anger melted. He said, "You fortified Shitou to rival me—yet today you come begging my pardon?"

sentences.zh: 」即與之談宴終日，遂與亮、嶠同趣建康。

translations.literal: " He then talked and feasted with him the whole day, and afterward marched with Liang and Jiao toward Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: " They talked and feasted all day, then marched with Liang and Jiao toward Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 戎卒四萬，旌旗七百餘里，鉦鼓之聲，震於遠近。

translations.literal: Armed soldiers numbered forty thousand; banners and flags stretched seven hundred li; the sound of gongs and drums shook near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Forty thousand soldiers marched under banners stretching seven hundred li; gongs and drums thundered across the land.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻聞西方兵起，用參軍賈寧計，自姑孰還據石頭，分兵以拒侃等。

translations.literal: Su Jun heard that armies had risen in the west and, adopting staff officer Jia Ning's plan, returned from Gushu to hold Shitou and divided his forces to resist Kan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun heard of the western armies, he followed staff officer Jia Ning's advice, withdrew from Gushu to Shitou, and divided his forces to block Kan and the allies.

sentences.zh: 乙未，峻逼遷帝於石頭。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Jun forced the emperor to move to Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Jun forced the emperor to relocate to Shitou.

sentences.zh: 司徒導固爭，不從。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor Dao argued firmly but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor Wang Dao protested fiercely but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 帝哀泣升車，宮中慟哭。

translations.literal: The emperor wept in grief as he mounted the carriage; within the palace there was loud mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as he boarded the carriage; the palace echoed with wailing.

sentences.zh: 時天大雨，道路泥濘，劉超、鐘雅步侍左右。

translations.literal: It rained heavily; the roads were mire; Liu Chao and Zhong Ya walked in attendance at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Rain poured down and the roads were mud; Liu Chao and Zhong Ya walked beside the carriage.

sentences.zh: 峻給馬，不肯乘，而悲哀慷慨。

translations.literal: Jun offered horses; they refused to ride and were mournful and impassioned.
translations.idiomatic: Jun offered horses; they refused and walked on, grief and defiance plain in their bearing.

sentences.zh: 峻聞而惡之，然未敢殺也。

translations.literal: Jun heard of this and hated them, yet did not dare kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Jun hated them for it but did not dare kill them.

sentences.zh: 以其親信許方等補司馬督、殿中監，外托宿衛，內實防禦超等。

translations.literal: He appointed his trusted followers Xu Fang and others to fill the posts of Director of the Masters of Horse and Palace Director, outwardly as palace guards but inwardly to guard against Chao and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He installed his confidant Xu Fang and others as palace guards, ostensibly to protect the emperor but in fact to watch Chao and his companions.

sentences.zh: 峻以倉屋為帝宮，日來帝前肆丑言。

translations.literal: Jun used a granary building as the imperial palace and came daily before the emperor to utter vile words.
translations.idiomatic: Jun housed the emperor in a granary and came each day to heap abuse on him.

sentences.zh: 劉超、鐘雅與右光祿大夫荀崧、金紫光祿大夫華恆、尚書荀邃、侍中丁潭侍從，不離帝側。

translations.literal: Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Right Household Counsellor Xun Song, Golden Purple-Glow Household Counsellor Hua Heng, Secretary Xun Sui, and Palace Attendant Ding Tan attended him and did not leave the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Xun Song, Hua Heng, Xun Sui, and Ding Tan never left the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 時饑饉，米貴，峻問遺，超一無所受，繾綣朝夕，臣節愈恭；

translations.literal: There was famine then and rice was dear; Jun sent gifts of food, but Chao accepted nothing, attending morning and evening with devoted care, his ministerial deportment ever more respectful;
translations.idiomatic: Famine made rice costly; Jun sent provisions, but Chao accepted nothing and attended the emperor morning and night with ever greater devotion;

sentences.zh: 雖居幽厄之中，超猶啟帝，授《孝經》、《論語》。

translations.literal: though living in dire straits, Chao still instructed the emperor, teaching him the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: even in captivity Chao continued to instruct the emperor in the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 峻使左光祿大夫陸曄守留台，逼近居民，盡聚之後苑；

translations.literal: Jun had Left Household Counsellor Lu Ye guard the remaining offices, pressed close upon the residents, and gathered them all into the rear park;
translations.idiomatic: Jun set Lu Ye to guard the remaining offices, drove nearby residents together, and herded them into the rear park;

sentences.zh: 使匡術守苑城。

translations.literal: he had Kuang Shu guard the park city.
translations.idiomatic: and put Kuang Shu in charge of the park fortress.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞孔坦奔陶侃，侃以為長史。

translations.literal: Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing Kong Tan fled to Tao Kan, and Kan made him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Kong Tan fled to Tao Kan, who made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 初，蘇峻遣尚書張闓權督東軍，司徒導密令以太后詔諭三吳吏士，使起義兵救天子。

translations.literal: Earlier, Su Jun had sent Secretary Zhang Kai to oversee the eastern armies with full authority; Grand Mentor Dao secretly ordered that the empress dowager's edict be used to instruct the officials and gentry of the Three Wu regions to raise righteous troops to rescue the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Su Jun had sent Zhang Kai to command the eastern armies; Grand Mentor Wang Dao secretly used the empress dowager's edict to call the Three Wu regions to arms for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會稽內史王舒以庾冰行奮武將軍，使將兵一萬，西渡浙江。

translations.literal: Kuaiji interior administrator Wang Shu had Yu Bing act as General of Inspiring Martiality and sent him to lead ten thousand troops west across the Zhe River.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji administrator Wang Shu sent Yu Bing as acting General of Inspiring Martiality with ten thousand men west across the Zhe River.

sentences.zh: 於是吳興太守虞潭、吳國內史蔡謨、前義興太守顧從等皆舉兵應之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wu Commandery grand administrator Yu Tan, Wu interior administrator Cai Mo, former Yixing grand administrator Gu Cong, and others all raised troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Commandery administrator Yu Tan, Wu interior administrator Cai Mo, former Yixing administrator Gu Cong, and others all rose in answer.

sentences.zh: 潭母孫氏謂譚曰：「汝當捨生取義，勿以吾老為累！

translations.literal: Tan’s mother, the Lady Sun, said to Tan: "You should give your life for righteousness; do not let my old age be a burden!"
translations.idiomatic: Tan's mother Lady Sun told him, "Give your life for the right cause—do not let my age hold you back!"

sentences.zh: 」盡遣其家僮從軍，鬻其環珮以為軍資。

translations.literal: " She sent out all her household servants to join the army and sold her rings and pendants for military funds.
translations.idiomatic: " She sent every household servant to the army and sold her jewelry for war funds.

sentences.zh: 謨以庾冰當還舊任，即去郡以讓冰。

translations.literal: Mo held that Yu Bing ought to return to his former post and at once left the commandery to yield it to Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo resigned his post immediately so Bing could resume his former command.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻聞東方兵起，遣其將管商、張健、弘徽等拒之；

translations.literal: Su Jun heard that armies had risen in the east and sent his generals Guan Shang, Zhang Jian, Hong Hui, and others to resist them;
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun heard of the eastern uprising, he sent Guan Shang, Zhang Jian, Hong Hui, and others to oppose it;

sentences.zh: 虞潭等與戰，互有勝負，未能得前。

translations.literal: Yu Tan and the others fought them with alternating victories and defeats and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan and the allies fought them to a standstill and could not break through.

sentences.zh: 陶侃、溫嶠軍於茄子浦；

translations.literal: Tao Kan and Wen Jiao encamped at Qiezi Ford;
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan and Wen Jiao encamped at Qiezi Ford;

sentences.zh: 嶠以南兵習水，蘇峻兵便步，令將士：「有上岸者死！

translations.literal: Jiao said that southern troops were skilled on water while Su Jun's men were adept on foot, and ordered the officers and soldiers: "Whoever goes ashore dies!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiao said the southern armies knew water while Su Jun's men fought best on land, and ordered: "Anyone who goes ashore dies!"

sentences.zh: 」會峻送米萬斛饋祖約，約遣司馬桓撫等迎之。

translations.literal: " It happened that Jun sent ten thousand hu of rice as a gift to Zu Yue; Yue sent Staff Officer Huan Fu and others to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun was sending ten thousand hu of rice to Zu Yue; Yue sent Staff Officer Huan Fu and others to fetch it.

sentences.zh: 毛寶帥千人為嶠前鋒，告其眾曰：「兵法：『軍令有所不從』，豈可視賊可擊，不上岸擊之邪！

translations.literal: Mao Bao led a thousand men as Jiao's vanguard and told his troops: "In the art of war, 'there are commands one may disobey'—how can we see the enemy can be struck and not go ashore to strike!"
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao led a thousand men as vanguard and told his troops, "The art of war says some orders may be disobeyed—how can we see the enemy vulnerable and not attack ashore!"

sentences.zh: 」乃擅往襲撫，悉獲其米，斬獲萬計，約由是饑乏。

translations.literal: " He then went on his own authority to attack Fu, seized all the rice, and killed and captured by the tens of thousands; Yue thereafter suffered famine and want.
translations.idiomatic: " He attacked on his own, seized all the grain, and killed or captured tens of thousands; Yue's army soon went hungry.

sentences.zh: 嶠表寶為廬江太守。

translations.literal: Jiao memorialized to make Bao grand administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao recommended Bao for appointment as Lujiang administrator.

sentences.zh: 陶侃表王舒監浙東軍事，虞潭監浙西軍事，郗鑒都督揚州八郡諸軍事，令舒、潭皆受鑒節度。

translations.literal: Tao Kan memorialized Wang Shu to oversee military affairs east of the Zhe, Yu Tan to oversee military affairs west of the Zhe, and Xi Jian to command all military affairs of the eight Yangzhou commanderies, ordering Shu and Tan both to accept Jian's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan appointed Wang Shu to command forces east of the Zhe, Yu Tan west of the Zhe, and Xi Jian to direct eight Yangzhou commanderies, with Shu and Tan under Jian's orders.

sentences.zh: 鑒帥眾渡江，與侃等會與於茄子浦，雍州刺史魏該亦以兵會之。

translations.literal: Jian led his host across the river and joined Kan and the others at Qiezi Ford; Yong Province inspector Wei Gai also came with troops to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Jian crossed the river with his army and joined Kan at Qiezi Ford; Yong Province inspector Wei Gai brought his troops as well.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，侃等舟師直指石頭，至於蔡洲，侃屯查浦，嶠屯沙門浦。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Kan and the others' fleet pointed straight at Shitou, reaching Cai Isle; Kan encamped at Zhapu and Jiao at Shamen Ford.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the allied fleet sailed straight for Shitou and reached Cai Isle; Kan camped at Zhapu and Jiao at Shamen Ford.

sentences.zh: 峻登烽火樓，望見士眾之盛，有懼色，謂左右曰：「吾本知溫嶠能得眾也。

translations.literal: Jun ascended the beacon tower, saw the mass of troops, showed fear, and said to those beside him, "I knew all along that Wen Jiao could win men's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Jun climbed the beacon tower, saw the allied host, and paled. He told his men, "I always knew Wen Jiao could rally the armies."

sentences.zh: 庾亮遣督護王彰擊峻黨張曜，反為所敗。

translations.literal: Yu Liang sent Supervisor Wang Zhang to attack Jun partisan Zhang Yao and was in turn defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang sent Supervisor Wang Zhang against Jun's follower Zhang Yao and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 亮送節傳以謝侃，侃答曰：「古人三敗，君侯始二；

translations.literal: Liang sent his insignia of office to apologize to Kan; Kan replied, "The ancients were defeated thrice—you, my lord, are only at two;
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent his seal of office to apologize; Kan replied, "The ancients lost three battles—you have only lost two;

sentences.zh: 當今事急，不宜數爾。

translations.literal: the present affair is urgent and this should not happen often."
translations.idiomatic: the crisis is too grave for repeated apologies."

sentences.zh: 」亮司馬陳郡殷融詣侃謝曰：「將軍為此，非融等所裁。

translations.literal: " Liang's staff officer Yin Rong of Chen commandery went to Kan to apologize and said, "The general did this—it was not within Rong and the others to decide."
translations.idiomatic: " Liang's aide Yin Rong came to apologize: "The general acted on his own—this was not our decision."

sentences.zh: 」王彰至曰：「彰自為之，將軍不知也。

translations.literal: " When Wang Zhang arrived he said, "Zhang did this on his own—the general did not know."
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Zhang then said, "I acted on my own—the general knew nothing."

sentences.zh: 」侃曰：「昔殷融為君子，王彰為小人；

translations.literal: " Kan said, "Formerly Yin Rong was the gentleman and Wang Zhang the petty man;
translations.idiomatic: " Kan said, "Once Yin Rong was the gentleman and Wang Zhang the scoundrel;

sentences.zh: 今王彰為君子，殷融為小人。

translations.literal: now Wang Zhang is the gentleman and Yin Rong the petty man."
translations.idiomatic: now Wang Zhang is the gentleman and Yin Rong the scoundrel."

sentences.zh: 宣城內史桓彝，聞京城不守，慷慨流涕，進屯涇縣。

translations.literal: Xuancheng interior administrator Huan Yi, on hearing that the capital could not be held, wept in impassioned grief and advanced to encamp at Jing county.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Yi, Xuancheng administrator, heard the capital had fallen, he wept openly and marched to Jing county.

sentences.zh: 時州郡多遣使降蘇峻，裨惠復勸彝宜且與通使，以紓交至之禍。

translations.literal: At the time many provinces and commanderies sent envoys to surrender to Su Jun; Pi Hui again urged Yi that he ought for the moment to exchange envoys to ease the disaster of imminent attack.
translations.idiomatic: Many provinces were sending envoys to surrender; Pi Hui urged Yi to open talks with Jun to stave off immediate attack.

sentences.zh: 彝曰：「吾受國厚恩，義在致死，焉能忍恥與逆臣通問！

translations.literal: Yi said, "I have received the state's deep grace; my duty is to die for it—how can I bear the shame of exchanging messages with a rebel minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The state has honored me deeply; my duty is to die for it—how can I shame myself by treating with a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 如其不濟，此則命也。

translations.literal: If it does not succeed, that is fate."
translations.idiomatic: If I fail, that is fate."

sentences.zh: 」彝遣將軍俞縱守蘭石，峻遣其將韓晃攻之。

translations.literal: " Yi sent General Yu Zong to hold Lanshi; Jun sent his general Han Huang to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi sent General Yu Zong to hold Lanshi; Jun sent Han Huang to attack him.

sentences.zh: 縱將敗，左右勸縱退軍。

translations.literal: Zong was on the verge of defeat; those beside him urged him to withdraw his army.
translations.idiomatic: As Zong's line was breaking, his men urged retreat.

sentences.zh: 縱曰：「吾受桓侯厚恩，當以死報。

translations.literal: Zong said, "I have received Lord Huan's deep grace and should repay it with death."
translations.idiomatic: Zong said, "Lord Huan has shown me great favor; I owe him my life."

sentences.zh: 吾之不可負桓侯，猶桓侯之不負國也。

translations.literal: That I cannot fail Lord Huan is like Lord Huan's not failing the state."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot betray him any more than he can betray the state."

sentences.zh: 」遂力戰而死。

translations.literal: " He then fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 晃進軍攻彝，六月，城陷，執彝，殺之。

translations.literal: Huang advanced to attack Yi; in the sixth month the city fell, Yi was seized, and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang then besieged Yi; in the sixth month the city fell, Yi was captured, and executed.

sentences.zh: 諸軍初至石頭，即欲決戰，陶侃曰：「賊眾方盛，難與爭鋒，當以歲月，智計破之。

translations.literal: When the various armies first reached Shitou they wished at once to give decisive battle; Tao Kan said, "The rebel host is at its height and hard to meet in the clash; we should use time and stratagem to break them."
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies first reached Shitou they wanted a decisive battle; Tao Kan said, "The rebels are at their peak—we must wear them down with time and strategy."

sentences.zh: 」既而屢戰無功，監軍部將李根請築白石壘，侃從之。

translations.literal: " After repeated battles without success, supervising-army section general Li Gen asked to build a fortress at Baishi, and Kan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " After several failed assaults, supervising general Li Gen proposed building a fort at Baishi, and Kan agreed.

sentences.zh: 夜築壘，至曉而成。

translations.literal: They built the fortress by night, and by dawn it was complete.
translations.idiomatic: They built it overnight; by dawn it stood complete.

sentences.zh: 聞峻軍嚴聲，諸將咸懼其來攻。

translations.literal: Hearing Jun's army in strict array, the generals all feared it would come to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Jun's troops mustering, the generals feared an immediate assault.

sentences.zh: 孔坦曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Kong Tan said, "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan said, "Not so."

sentences.zh: 若峻攻壘，必須東北風急，令我水軍不得往救；

translations.literal: If Jun were to attack the fortress, there would have to be a fierce northeast wind so that our water forces could not go to the rescue;
translations.idiomatic: If Jun meant to attack the fort, he would need a fierce northeast wind to keep our fleet from helping;

sentences.zh: 今天清靜，賊必不來。

translations.literal: today the sky is clear and calm—the rebels surely will not come.
translations.idiomatic: the sky is clear today—the rebels will not come.

sentences.zh: 所以嚴者，必遣軍出江乘，掠京口以東矣。

translations.literal: The reason for the strict array must be that he is sending troops out through Jiangcheng to raid east of Jingkou."
translations.idiomatic: They are mustering because he is sending troops through Jiangcheng to raid east of Jingkou."

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: " And so it proved.
translations.idiomatic: " He was right.

sentences.zh: 侃使庾亮以二千人守白石，峻帥步騎萬餘四面攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Kan had Yu Liang hold Baishi with two thousand men; Jun led more than ten thousand foot and horse and attacked on four sides but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Kan left Yu Liang with two thousand men at Baishi; Jun attacked with over ten thousand infantry and cavalry from all sides but failed.

sentences.zh: 王舒、虞潭等數與峻兵戰，不利。

translations.literal: Wang Shu, Yu Tan, and others fought Jun's troops several times without success.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu and Yu Tan fought Jun's forces repeatedly without success.

sentences.zh: 孔坦曰：「本不須召郗公，遂使東門無限。

translations.literal: Kong Tan said, "We need not have summoned Lord Xi in the first place, and thus left the eastern gate without limit."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan said, "We should never have summoned Xi Jian and left the eastern front uncovered."

sentences.zh: 今宜遣還，雖晚，猶勝不也。

translations.literal: Now we ought to send him back; though late, it is still better than not doing so."
translations.idiomatic: Send him back now—late as it is, that is still better than leaving him here."

sentences.zh: 」侃乃令鑒與後將軍郭默還據京口，立大業、曲阿、庱亭三壘以分峻之兵勢，使郭默守大業。

translations.literal: " Kan then ordered Jian and Rear General Guo Mo to return and hold Jingkou, establishing three fortresses at Daye, Qu'a, and Chanting to divide Jun's military strength, and had Guo Mo guard Daye.
translations.idiomatic: " Kan sent Jian and Rear General Guo Mo back to hold Jingkou, building forts at Daye, Qu'a, and Chanting to divide Jun's forces, with Guo Mo at Daye.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，魏該卒。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Wei Gai died.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Wei Gai died.

sentences.zh: 祖約遣祖渙、桓撫襲湓口。

translations.literal: Zu Yue sent Zu Huan and Huan Fu to raid Penkou.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue sent Zu Huan and Huan Fu to raid Penkou.

sentences.zh: 陶侃聞之，將自擊之。

translations.literal: When Tao Kan heard of it he was about to strike them himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan heard and prepared to attack them himself.

sentences.zh: 毛寶曰：「義軍恃公，公不可動，寶請討之。

translations.literal: Mao Bao said, "The righteous army relies on you, sir—you must not move; Bao asks leave to punish them."
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao said, "The allied army depends on you—you must not leave; let me go."

sentences.zh: 」侃從之。

translations.literal: " Kan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Kan agreed.

sentences.zh: 渙、撫過皖，因攻譙國內史桓宣。

translations.literal: Huan and Fu passed Wan and thereupon attacked Qiao interior administrator Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan and Fu passed Wan and attacked Qiao administrator Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 寶往救之，為渙、撫所敗。

translations.literal: Bao went to rescue him and was defeated by Huan and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Bao went to his aid and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 箭貫寶髀，徹鞍，寶使人蹋鞍拔箭，血流滿靴。

translations.literal: An arrow pierced Bao's thigh and went through the saddle; Bao had a man step on the saddle to pull out the arrow, and blood filled his boots.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow pierced his thigh and the saddle; he had a man stand on the saddle to pull it out, and blood filled his boots.

sentences.zh: 還擊渙、撫，破走之，宣乃得出，歸於溫嶠。

translations.literal: He turned back to strike Huan and Fu, routed them, and Xuan was then able to get out and join Wen Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: He counterattacked, routed them, and Xuan escaped to join Wen Jiao.

sentences.zh: 寶進攻祖約軍於東關，拔合肥戍，會嶠召之，復歸石頭。

translations.literal: Bao advanced to attack Zu Yue's army at Dongguan, took the Hefei garrison, and when Jiao summoned him returned again to Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Bao attacked Yue's army at Dongguan and took the Hefei garrison, then returned to Shitou when Jiao recalled him.

sentences.zh: 祖約諸將陰與後趙通謀，許為內應。

translations.literal: Several of Zu Yue's generals secretly communicated with Later Zhao in conspiracy and promised to act as inner agents.
translations.idiomatic: Several of Zu Yue's generals secretly plotted with Later Zhao to act as inside collaborators.

sentences.zh: 後趙將石聰，石堪引兵濟淮，攻壽春。

translations.literal: Later Zhao generals Shi Cong and Shi Kan led troops across the Huai to attack Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao generals Shi Cong and Shi Kan crossed the Huai and attacked Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，約眾潰，奔歷陽，聰等虜壽春二萬餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Yue's host collapsed and fled to Liyang; Cong and the others carried off more than twenty thousand households of Shouchun and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Yue's army collapsed and fled to Liyang; Cong and the others carried off more than twenty thousand Shouchun households and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後趙中山公虎帥眾四萬自軹關西入，擊趙河東。

translations.literal: Later Zhao Duke of Zhongshan Shi Hu led forty thousand troops through Zhi Pass from the west and attacked Zhao's Hedong region.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao Duke of Zhongshan Shi Hu led forty thousand men west through Zhi Pass and struck at Zhao's Hedong region.

sentences.zh: 應之者五十餘縣，遂進攻蒲阪。

translations.literal: More than fifty counties responded; he then advanced to attack Puban.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty counties answered his call, and he pressed on to attack Puban.

sentences.zh: 趙主曜遣河間王述發氐、羌之眾屯秦州以備張駿、楊難敵，自將中外精銳水陸諸軍以救蒲阪，自衛關北濟；

translations.literal: Zhao's ruler Liu Yao sent Prince of Hejian Liu Shu to mobilize Di and Qiang forces to garrison Qin Province against Zhang Jun and Yang Nandi, while he personally led elite forces from inside and outside the court, both land and naval, to relieve Puban, crossing north from Wei Pass;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's ruler Liu Yao sent Prince of Hejian Liu Shu to raise Di and Qiang troops and hold Qin Province against Zhang Jun and Yang Nandi, while he himself led the court's finest land and river forces to relieve Puban, crossing north from Wei Pass;

sentences.zh: 虎懼，引退。

translations.literal: Hu was afraid and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was frightened and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 曜追之，八月，及於高候，與虎戰，大破之，斬石瞻；

translations.literal: Yao pursued him; in the eighth month he caught up at Gaohou, fought Hu, routed him utterly, and beheaded Shi Zhan;
translations.idiomatic: Yao pursued; in the eighth month he caught Hu at Gaohou, fought a great battle, shattered his army, and beheaded Shi Zhan;

sentences.zh: 枕屍二百餘里，收其資仗億計，虎奔朝歌。

translations.literal: The dead piled up for more than two hundred li; he seized arms and equipment numbering in the hundreds of millions; Hu fled to Chaoge.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses lay stacked for more than two hundred li; he took arms and gear beyond counting; Hu fled to Chaoge.

sentences.zh: 曜濟自大陽，攻石生於金墉，決千金堨以灌之。

translations.literal: Yao crossed from Dayang and attacked Shi Sheng at Jinyong, breaching the Qianjin dyke to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yao crossed from Dayang and attacked Shi Sheng at Jinyong, breaking the Qianjin dyke to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 分遣諸將攻汲郡、河內，後趙滎陽太守尹矩、野王太守張進等皆降之。

translations.literal: He dispatched generals to attack Ji Prefecture and Henei; Yin Ju, Later Zhao's governor of Xingyang, Zhang Jin, governor of Yewang, and others all surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent generals against Ji Prefecture and Henei; Yin Ju, Later Zhao's governor of Xingyang, Zhang Jin, governor of Yewang, and others all submitted.

sentences.zh: 襄國大震。

translations.literal: Xiangguo was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangguo was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 張駿治兵，欲乘虛襲長安。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun mustered troops, intending to strike Chang'an while the enemy was exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun gathered his army, planning to exploit the opening and strike Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 理曹郎中索詢諫曰：「劉曜雖東征，其子胤守長安，未易輕也。

translations.literal: Court Gentleman Su Xun of the Bureau of Justice remonstrated: "Though Liu Yao has gone east on campaign, his son Yin holds Chang'an—it is not to be taken lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Court Gentleman Su Xun of the Bureau of Justice remonstrated: "Though Liu Yao is campaigning in the east, his son Yin still holds Chang'an. The city is not to be taken lightly.

sentences.zh: 借使小有所獲，彼若釋東方之圖，還與我校；

translations.literal: Even if we gain a little, if he abandons his plans in the east and turns to fight us—
translations.idiomatic: Even if we win a small gain, should he abandon his eastern campaign and turn to fight us—

sentences.zh: 禍難之期，未可量也」駿乃止。

translations.literal: when disaster might strike cannot be foreseen." Zhang Jun then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: no one can say when calamity would fall." Zhang Jun then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻腹心路永、匡術、賈寧聞祖約敗，恐事不濟，勸峻盡誅司徒導等諸大臣，更樹腹心；

translations.literal: Su Jun's confidants Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, and Jia Ning, hearing that Zu Yue had been defeated and fearing the cause would fail, urged Jun to execute all the senior ministers including Grand Tutor Wang Dao and install new trusted men;
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun's inner circle—Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, and Jia Ning—heard that Zu Yue had been beaten and, fearing the enterprise would collapse, urged Jun to kill all the chief ministers, including Grand Tutor Wang Dao, and raise a new set of trusted men;

sentences.zh: 峻雅敬導，不許。

translations.literal: Jun had always held Dao in respect and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had always held Dao in esteem and refused.

sentences.zh: 永等更貳於峻，導使參軍袁耽潛誘永歸順。

translations.literal: Yong and the others again turned against Jun; Dao sent his staff officer Yuan Dan to secretly win Yong over to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and the others again wavered toward Jun; Dao sent his staff officer Yuan Dan to win Yong over in secret.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊申，導攜二子與永皆奔白石。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wushen, Dao took his two sons and fled with Yong to Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wushen, Dao took his two sons and fled with Yong to Baishi.

sentences.zh: 耽，渙之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Dan was a great-grandson of Yuan Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was a great-grandson of Yuan Huan.

sentences.zh: 陶侃、溫嶠等與蘇峻久相持不決，峻分遣諸將東西攻掠，所向多捷，人情心匈懼。

translations.literal: Tao Kan, Wen Jiao, and the others had been locked in stalemate with Su Jun for a long time; Jun dispatched generals east and west to raid and plunder, succeeding wherever they went, and men's hearts were filled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan, Wen Jiao, and the others had been deadlocked with Su Jun for a long time; Jun sent generals east and west to raid, winning almost everywhere they went, and fear spread through every heart.

sentences.zh: 朝士之奔西軍者皆曰：「峻狡黠有膽決，其徒驍勇，所向無敵。

translations.literal: Court officials who had fled to the western army all said: "Jun is cunning and bold; his followers are fierce—none can stand against them.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials who had fled to the western army kept saying: "Jun is cunning and resolute, his men are fierce—nothing can stop them.

sentences.zh: 若天討有罪，則峻終滅亡；

translations.literal: If Heaven punishes guilt, Jun will perish in the end;
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven punishes the guilty, Jun will be destroyed in the end;

sentences.zh: 止以人事言之，未易除也。

translations.literal: but judged by human affairs alone, he is not easily removed."
translations.idiomatic: but judged by human strength alone, he will not be easy to remove."

sentences.zh: 」溫嶠怒曰：「諸君怯懦，乃更譽賊！

translations.literal: " Wen Jiao flared in anger: "You are all cowards—and you praise the rebel!
translations.idiomatic: " Wen Jiao burst out in anger: "You are cowards—and you praise the rebel!

sentences.zh: 」及累戰不勝，嶠亦憚之。

translations.literal: " After repeated defeats, Jiao too came to fear him.
translations.idiomatic: " After one defeat after another, Jiao too began to fear him.

sentences.zh: 嶠軍食盡，貸於陶侃。

translations.literal: Jiao's army ran out of grain and borrowed from Tao Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's army ran out of food and asked Tao Kan for supplies.

sentences.zh: 侃怒曰：「使君前雲不憂無良將及兵食，惟欲得老僕為主耳。

translations.literal: Kan said angrily: "You, my lord, said before you did not worry about lacking good generals or provisions—you only wanted this old servant as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Kan said angrily: "You said before that you had no worry about good generals or grain—you only wanted this old servant to take command.

sentences.zh: 今數戰皆北，良將安在！

translations.literal: Now battle after battle ends in defeat—where are those good generals!
translations.idiomatic: Now you have lost battle after battle—where are those good generals!

sentences.zh: 荊州接胡、蜀二虜，當備不虞；

translations.literal: Jing Province borders the barbarians of Hu and Shu; we must guard against the unexpected;
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province faces the Hu and Shu barbarians on two sides; we must stay ready for surprise;

sentences.zh: 若復無食，僕便欲西歸，更思良算。

translations.literal: if we run out of grain again, this servant means to go west and devise a better plan.
translations.idiomatic: if we run short of grain again, I mean to go west and think of a better plan.

sentences.zh: 徐來殄賊，不為晚也。

translations.literal: We can destroy the rebels in time—it will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: We can still wipe out the rebels in good time—it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 」嶠曰：「凡師克在和，古之善教也。

translations.literal: " Jiao said: "Victory in any army depends on harmony—that is ancient wisdom well taught.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiao said: "Every army wins through unity—that is what the ancients taught best.

sentences.zh: 光武之濟昆陽，曹公之拔官渡，以寡敵眾，杖義故也。

translations.literal: Guangwu's relief of Kunyang and Cao Gong's capture of Guandu—both overcame many with few because they wielded righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu's rescue at Kunyang and Cao Gong's victory at Guandu—both used the few against the many because they stood on righteousness.

sentences.zh: 峻、約小豎，凶逆滔天，何憂不滅！

translations.literal: Jun and Yue are petty upstarts, their treachery reaching heaven—why worry they will not be destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Yue are petty rebels whose crimes reach heaven—why doubt they can be destroyed!

sentences.zh: 峻驟勝而驕，自謂無前，今挑之戰，可一鼓而擒也。

translations.literal: Jun's sudden victories have made him arrogant; he thinks himself unmatched—provoke him now and we can take him in one assault.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's streak of victories has made him arrogant; he thinks himself invincible. Provoke him now and we can take him at one stroke.

sentences.zh: 奈何捨垂立之功，設進退之計乎！

translations.literal: Why abandon a victory within reach and talk of advance and retreat!
translations.idiomatic: Why throw away a victory within reach and talk of advancing and retreating!

sentences.zh: 且天子幽逼，社稷危殆，乃四海臣子肝腦塗地之日。

translations.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven is held in duress and the altars of state are in peril—this is the day when subjects throughout the realm should spill heart and brain upon the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is held captive and the altars of state are in peril—this is the day when every subject in the realm should lay down life and limb.

sentences.zh: 嶠等與公並受國恩，事若克濟，則臣主同祚；

translations.literal: Jiao and the rest have received the state's grace together with you; if the affair succeeds, lord and ministers share fortune;
translations.idiomatic: You and I alike have received the state's grace; if we succeed, lord and ministers share the reward;

sentences.zh: 如其不捷，當灰身以謝先帝耳。

translations.literal: if it fails, we ought to burn our bodies to atone before the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: if we fail, we should burn our bodies to answer to the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 今之事勢，義無旋踵，譬如騎虎，安可中下哉！

translations.literal: The situation now brooks no turning back—like riding a tiger, how can one dismount halfway!
translations.idiomatic: The situation now allows no turning back—like riding a tiger, how can one get off halfway!

sentences.zh: 公若違眾獨返，人心必沮；

translations.literal: If you defy the host and return alone, hearts will surely sink;
translations.idiomatic: If you go against the host and return alone, every heart will sink;

sentences.zh: 沮眾敗事，義旗將回指於公矣。

translations.literal: once spirits fail and the cause collapses, the banner of righteousness will turn against you."
translations.idiomatic: once morale breaks and the cause fails, the banner of righteousness will turn on you."

sentences.zh: 」毛寶言於嶠曰：「下官能留陶公。

translations.literal: " Mao Bao said to Jiao: "Your humble officer can keep Lord Tao.
translations.idiomatic: " Mao Bao said to Jiao: "Your humble officer can keep Lord Tao here.

sentences.zh: 」乃往說侃曰：「公本應鎮蕪湖，為南北勢援，前既已下，勢不可還。

translations.literal: " He then went to persuade Kan: "You were meant to hold Wuhu as the linchpin between north and south; having come down already, you cannot turn back.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went to Kan and said: "You were meant to hold Wuhu as the pivot between north and south. Having come down already, you cannot turn back.

sentences.zh: 且軍政有進無退，非直整齊三軍，示眾必死而已，亦謂退無所據，終至滅亡。

translations.literal: And in military affairs one advances, never retreats—not only to array the three armies and show all they must die, but because retreat leaves nowhere to stand and ends in destruction.
translations.idiomatic: In war one advances, never retreats—not only to drill the three armies and show that all must die, but because retreat leaves nowhere to stand and ends in ruin.

sentences.zh: 往者杜弢非不強盛，公竟滅之，何至於峻，獨不可破邪！

translations.literal: Du Tao was not without power; you destroyed him in the end—why should Jun alone be unbreakable!
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao was no weak foe, yet you destroyed him in the end—why should Jun alone be impossible to break!

sentences.zh: 賊亦畏死，非皆勇健，公可試與寶兵，使上岸斷賊資糧。

translations.literal: The rebels fear death too; not all are brave—give Bao troops and let him go ashore to cut their supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fear death too; not all are heroes. Give Bao troops and let him go ashore to cut their grain.

sentences.zh: 若寶不立效，然後公去，人心不恨矣。

translations.literal: If Bao fails, then you may leave—and no one will blame you."
translations.idiomatic: If Bao fails, then you may leave—and no one will resent you."

sentences.zh: 」侃然之，加寶督護而遣之。

translations.literal: " Kan agreed, made Bao superintendent of defense, and sent him.
translations.idiomatic: " Kan agreed, made Bao superintendent of defense, and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 竟陵太守李陽說侃曰：「今大事若不濟，公雖有粟，安得而食諸！

translations.literal: " Jingling Governor Li Yang said to Kan: "If the great undertaking fails now, though you have grain, who will eat it!
translations.idiomatic: " Jingling Governor Li Yang said to Kan: "If the great cause fails now, though you have grain, who will eat it!

sentences.zh: 」侃乃分米五萬石以餉嶠軍。

translations.literal: " Kan then divided out fifty thousand shi of rice to supply Jiao's army.
translations.idiomatic: " Kan then sent fifty thousand shi of rice to supply Jiao's army.

sentences.zh: 毛寶燒峻句容、湖孰積聚，峻軍乏食，侃遂留不去。

translations.literal: Mao Bao burned Jun's stockpiles at Jurong and Hushu; Jun's army ran short of food, and Kan stayed and did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao burned Jun's stores at Jurong and Hushu; Jun's army ran short of food, and Kan stayed.

sentences.zh: 張健、韓晃等急攻大業；

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, Han Huang, and others pressed hard against Daye;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, Han Huang, and others pressed the attack on Daye;

sentences.zh: 壘中乏水，人飲糞汁。

translations.literal: the fortress ran short of water and men drank foul drainage.
translations.idiomatic: inside the fortress water ran out and men drank foul drainage.

sentences.zh: 郭默懼，潛突圍出外，留兵守之。

translations.literal: Guo Mo was afraid; he slipped through the encirclement and got out, leaving troops to hold the place.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo was afraid; he broke out in secret and escaped, leaving troops to hold the fortress.

sentences.zh: 郗鑒在京口，軍士聞之皆失色。

translations.literal: Xi Jian was at Jingkou; when his soldiers heard of this they all turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian was at Jingkou; when his soldiers heard of it they all turned pale.

sentences.zh: 參軍曹納曰：「大業，京口之扞蔽也，一旦不守，則賊兵徑至，不可當也。

translations.literal: Staff officer Cao Na said: "Daye is Jingkou's shield; if it falls at once, rebel troops will come straight through and cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Cao Na said: "Daye is Jingkou's shield. If it falls at once, rebel troops will come straight through and we cannot stop them.

sentences.zh: 請還廣陵，以俟後舉。

translations.literal: I ask that we withdraw to Guangling and await a future effort."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we fall back to Guangling and wait for a later move."

sentences.zh: 」鑒大會僚佐，責納曰：「吾受先帝顧托之重，正復捐軀九泉，不足報塞。

translations.literal: " Jian convened his officers and rebuked Na: "I bear the late emperor's weight of trust; even to give my body to the nine springs would not repay the debt.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian called his officers together and rebuked Na: "I bear the late emperor's charge of trust. Even to die and lie in the nine springs would not repay it.

sentences.zh: 今強寇在近，眾心危逼，君腹心之佐，而生長異端，當何以帥先義眾，鎮壹三軍邪！

translations.literal: Now the strong foe is near and every heart is pressed with peril—you are my closest aide, yet you sow discord; how am I to lead the righteous host and steady the three armies!
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy is close and every heart is in peril—you are my closest aide, yet you raise division. How am I to lead the loyal host and hold the three armies firm!

sentences.zh: 」將斬之，久乃得釋。

translations.literal: " He was about to behead him but after a long while was persuaded to release him.
translations.idiomatic: " He was about to behead him but at last was persuaded to spare him.

sentences.zh: 陶侃將救大業，長史殷羨曰：「吾兵不習步戰，救大業而不捷，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: Tao Kan was about to relieve Daye; Chief Administrator Yin Xian said: "Our troops are not trained for fighting on foot; if we fail to save Daye, the great cause is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan was about to relieve Daye; Chief Administrator Yin Xian said: "Our men are not used to fighting on foot. If we fail to save Daye, the great cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 不如急攻石頭，則大業自解。

translations.literal: Better to strike Shitou at once—then Daye will relieve itself."
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike Shitou at once—then Daye will free itself."

sentences.zh: 」侃從之。

translations.literal: " Kan followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Kan took his advice.

sentences.zh: 羨，融之兄也。

translations.literal: Xian was the elder brother of Yin Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was the elder brother of Yin Rong.

sentences.zh: 庚午，侃督水軍向石頭。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Kan led the river forces toward Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Kan led the river army toward Shitou.

sentences.zh: 庾亮、溫嶠、趙胤帥步兵萬人從白石南上，欲挑戰。

translations.literal: Yu Liang, Wen Jiao, and Zhao Yin led ten thousand foot soldiers south from Baishi, intending to provoke battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang, Wen Jiao, and Zhao Yin led ten thousand foot soldiers south from Baishi, seeking to draw the enemy out.

sentences.zh: 峻將八千人逆戰，遣其子碩及其將匡孝分兵先薄趙胤軍，敗之。

translations.literal: Jun's generals with eight thousand met them in battle; he sent his son Shuo and his general Kuang Xiao with divided forces to press Zhao Yin's army first and routed it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's generals, eight thousand strong, met them; he sent his son Shuo and his general Kuang Xiao with divided forces to press Zhao Yin's army first and broke it.

sentences.zh: 峻方勞其將士，乘醉望見胤走，曰：「孝能破賊，我更不如邪！

translations.literal: Jun was just entertaining his officers; drunk, he saw Yin fleeing and said: "If Xiao can break the enemy, am I not his better!
translations.idiomatic: Jun was just feasting his officers; drunk, he saw Yin fleeing and cried: "If Xiao can beat the enemy, am I not his better!

sentences.zh: 」因捨其眾，與數騎北下突陳，不得入，將回趨白木陂；

translations.literal: " He therefore abandoned his host, charged the line with only a few horsemen from the north, could not break through, and was turning toward Baimu Marsh;
translations.idiomatic: " He threw off his host, charged the line with only a few horsemen from the north, could not break through, and was turning toward Baimu Marsh;

sentences.zh: 馬躓，侃部將彭世、李千等投之以矛，峻墜馬；

translations.literal: his horse stumbled; Peng Shi, Li Qian, and other officers under Kan cast spears at him and Jun fell from his horse;
translations.idiomatic: his horse stumbled; Peng Shi, Li Qian, and other officers under Kan hurled spears at him and Jun fell from his horse;
