sentences.zh: 斬首，臠割之，焚其骨，三軍皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: they beheaded him, carved his flesh, burned his bones, and the whole army shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: they beheaded him, cut his flesh, burned his bones, and the whole army shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 餘眾大潰。

translations.literal: The remaining host collapsed in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 峻司馬任讓等共立峻弟逸為主，閉城自守。

translations.literal: Jun's marshal Ren Rang and others together installed Jun's younger brother Yi as leader and shut the city to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's marshal Ren Rang and others together set up Jun's younger brother Yi as leader and shut the city to hold it.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠乃立行台，佈告遠近，凡故吏二千石以下，皆令赴台，於是至者雲集。

translations.literal: Wen Jiao then established a provisional headquarters, announced it far and near, and ordered all former officials of the two-thousand-shi rank and below to come to the HQ; they gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao then set up a field headquarters, proclaimed it far and near, and ordered all former officials of two-thousand-shi rank and below to report; they came in crowds.

sentences.zh: 韓晃聞峻死，引兵趣石頭。

translations.literal: Han Huang, hearing that Jun was dead, led troops toward Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, hearing that Jun was dead, marched toward Shitou.

sentences.zh: 管商、弘徽攻庱亭壘，督護李閎、輕車長史滕含擊破之。

translations.literal: Guan Shang and Hong Hiao attacked the Chiting fortress; Superintendent Li Hong and Chariot Commandant Teng Han defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Shang and Hong Hiao attacked the Chiting fortress; Superintendent Li Hong and Chariot Commandant Teng Han beat them back.

sentences.zh: 含，修之孫也。

translations.literal: Han was a grandson of Teng Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Han was a grandson of Teng Xiu.

sentences.zh: 商走詣庾亮降，餘眾皆歸張健。

translations.literal: Shang fled to Yu Liang to surrender; the rest joined Zhang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Shang fled to Yu Liang and surrendered; the rest went over to Zhang Jian.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，後趙王勒欲自將救洛陽，僚佐程遐等固諫曰：「劉曜懸軍千里，勢不支久。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Later Zhao King Shi Le wished to go in person to relieve Luoyang; his aides Cheng Xia and others firmly remonstrated: "Liu Yao's army is a thousand li from home; the position cannot hold long.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, Later Zhao King Shi Le wished to go in person to relieve Luoyang; his aides Cheng Xia and others firmly remonstrated: "Liu Yao's army is a thousand li from home. The position cannot last.

sentences.zh: 大王不宜親動，動無萬全。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should not move in person—movement brings no sure success."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should not go in person—if you move, nothing is certain."

sentences.zh: 」勒大怒，按劍叱遐等出。

translations.literal: " Le flew into rage, laid hand on his sword, and shouted Xia and the others out.
translations.idiomatic: " Le flew into a rage, laid hand on his sword, and drove Xia and the others out.

sentences.zh: 乃赦徐光，召而謂之曰：「劉曜乘一戰之勝，圍守洛陽，庸人之情皆謂其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: He then pardoned Xu Guang, summoned him, and said: "Liu Yao rides one victory to besiege Luoyang; common minds all say his edge cannot be faced.
translations.idiomatic: He then pardoned Xu Guang, summoned him, and said: "Liu Yao rides one victory to besiege Luoyang. Ordinary minds all say his edge cannot be faced.

sentences.zh: 曜帶甲十萬，攻一城而百日不克，帥老卒怠，以我初銳擊之，可一戰而擒也。

translations.literal: Yao has armor by the hundred thousand yet cannot take one city in a hundred days—his commanders are old, his soldiers weary; strike with our fresh sharpness and we can take him in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yao has a hundred thousand armored men yet cannot take one city in a hundred days—his commanders are worn, his soldiers tired. Strike with our fresh edge and we can take him in one battle.

sentences.zh: 若洛陽不守，曜必送死冀州，自河已北，席捲而來，吾事去矣。

translations.literal: If Luoyang is not held, Yao will surely march to his death in Ji Province; from the Yellow River north he will sweep down—and our cause is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If Luoyang is not held, Yao will surely drive to his death in Ji Province; from the Yellow River north he will sweep down—and our cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 程遐等不欲吾行，卿以為何如？

translations.literal: Cheng Xia and the rest do not want me to go—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xia and the rest do not want me to go—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「劉曜乘高候之勢，不能進臨襄國，更守金墉，此其無能為可知也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Liu Yao, riding the momentum of Gaohou, could not advance on Xiangguo and instead holds Jinyong—his incapacity is plain.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Liu Yao, riding the victory at Gaohou, could not advance on Xiangguo and instead holds Jinyong—his weakness is plain.

sentences.zh: 以大王威略臨之，彼必望旗奔敗。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty's might and strategy come upon him, they will surely flee at sight of the banners.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty's might and strategy come upon him, they will surely break at sight of your banners.

sentences.zh: 平定天下，在今一舉，不可失也。

translations.literal: To settle the realm hangs on this one stroke—it must not be missed."
translations.idiomatic: To settle the realm hangs on this one stroke—it must not be missed."

sentences.zh: 」勒笑曰：「光言是也。

translations.literal: " Le laughed and said: "Guang speaks rightly.
translations.idiomatic: " Le laughed and said: "Guang is right.

sentences.zh: 」乃使內外戒嚴，有諫者斬。

translations.literal: " He then ordered alert throughout court and camp; whoever remonstrated was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered alert throughout court and camp; whoever remonstrated was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 命石堪、石聰及豫州刺史桃豹等各統見眾會滎陽；

translations.literal: He ordered Shi Kan, Shi Cong, and Yuzhou Inspector Tao Bao each to lead available troops and assemble at Xingyang;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Shi Kan, Shi Cong, and Yuzhou Inspector Tao Bao each to lead available troops and assemble at Xingyang;

sentences.zh: 中山公虎進據石門，勒自統步騎四萬趣金墉，濟自大堨。

translations.literal: Duke of Zhongshan Shi Hu advanced to hold Shimen; Le personally led forty thousand foot and horse toward Jinyong, crossing at the Great Dyke.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Zhongshan Shi Hu advanced to hold Shimen; Le personally led forty thousand foot and horse toward Jinyong, crossing at the Great Dyke.

sentences.zh: 勒謂徐光曰：「曜盛兵成皋關，上策也；

translations.literal: Le said to Xu Guang: "For Yao to mass troops at Chenggao Pass would be the best plan;
translations.idiomatic: Le said to Xu Guang: "If Yao massed troops at Chenggao Pass, that would be the best plan;

sentences.zh: 阻洛水，其次也；

translations.literal: to block the Luo River would be second;
translations.idiomatic: to block the Luo River would be second;

sentences.zh: 坐守洛陽，此成擒耳。

translations.literal: to sit and hold Luoyang—that means capture."
translations.idiomatic: to sit and hold Luoyang—that means he is ours for the taking."

sentences.zh: 」十二月，乙亥，後趙諸軍集於成皋，步卒六萬，騎二萬七千。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month, on yihai, Later Zhao's armies gathered at Chenggao: sixty thousand foot soldiers and twenty-seven thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month, on yihai, Later Zhao's armies gathered at Chenggao: sixty thousand foot soldiers and twenty-seven thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 勒見趙無守兵，大喜，舉手指天，復加額，曰：「天也！

translations.literal: Le saw that Zhao had no defending troops and was greatly pleased; he raised a finger to Heaven, then touched his forehead, and said: "Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Le saw that Zhao had no troops on guard and was greatly pleased; he pointed to Heaven, then touched his forehead, and said: "Heaven!

sentences.zh: 」卷甲銜枚，詭道兼行，出於鞏、訾之間。

translations.literal: " They rolled up armor, gagged mouths with wood, took secret routes by forced marches, and emerged between Gong and Zi.
translations.idiomatic: " They rolled up armor, gagged mouths with wood, marched by secret routes at forced pace, and came out between Gong and Zi.

sentences.zh: 趙主曜專與嬖臣飲博，不撫士卒；

translations.literal: Zhao's ruler Liu Yao devoted himself to drinking and gambling with favorite minions and did not comfort his soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's ruler Liu Yao spent his time drinking and gambling with favorite minions and did not look to his soldiers;

sentences.zh: 左右或諫，曜怒，以為妖言，斬之。

translations.literal: when attendants remonstrated, Yao grew angry, called it sorcery talk, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: when attendants remonstrated, Yao grew angry, called it sorcery, and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 聞勒已濟河，始議增滎陽戍，杜黃馬關。

translations.literal: When they heard that Le had already crossed the river, they only then began to discuss reinforcing the garrison at Xingyang and blocking the Du, Huangma, and Guan passes.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they heard that Shi Le had already crossed the river did they begin to discuss reinforcing the Xingyang garrison and sealing the Du, Huangma, and Guan passes.

sentences.zh: 俄而洛水候者與後趙前鋒交戰，擒羯送之。

translations.literal: Before long, scouts on the Luo River fought Later Zhao's vanguard, captured a Jie tribesman, and sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, Luo River scouts clashed with Later Zhao's vanguard, captured a Jie tribesman, and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 曜問：「大胡自來邪？

translations.literal: Yao asked: "Has the Great Barbarian come in person?
translations.idiomatic: Yao asked: "Has the Great Barbarian come in person?

sentences.zh: 其眾幾何？

translations.literal: How many are his troops?
translations.idiomatic: How large is his force?

sentences.zh: 」羯曰：「王自來，軍勢甚盛。

translations.literal: " The Jie tribesman said: "The king has come in person; his army's momentum is very strong.
translations.idiomatic: " The captive said: "The king has come in person, and his army's strength is overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 」曜色變，使攝金墉之圍，陳於洛西，眾十餘萬，南北十餘里。

translations.literal: " Yao's countenance changed; he ordered someone to take over the siege of Jinyong and formed battle lines west of the Luo, with more than a hundred thousand men arrayed for more than ten li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's face fell. He had someone take command of the siege of Jinyong and drew up his forces west of the Luo—more than a hundred thousand men spread over ten li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 勒望見，益喜，謂左右曰：「可以賀我矣！

translations.literal: Le saw them from afar and was all the more pleased; he said to those beside him: "You may congratulate me now!
translations.idiomatic: When Le saw them from afar he was delighted and said to those around him: "You may congratulate me now!

sentences.zh: 」勒帥步騎四萬入洛陽城。

translations.literal: " Le led forty thousand infantry and cavalry into Luoyang city.
translations.idiomatic: Le then led forty thousand infantry and cavalry into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 己卯，中山公虎引步卒三萬自城北而西，攻趙中軍，石堪、石聰等各以精騎八千自城西而北，擊趙前鋒，大戰於西陽門。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, Duke of Zhongshan Hu led thirty thousand foot soldiers from the north of the city westward to attack Zhao's center army; Shi Kan, Shi Cong, and others each led eight thousand elite cavalry from the west of the city northward to strike Zhao's vanguard; a great battle was fought at the Xiyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Duke of Zhongshan Hu led thirty thousand foot soldiers from the north wall westward against Zhao's center army, while Shi Kan, Shi Cong, and others each led eight thousand elite cavalry from the west wall northward to hit Zhao's vanguard. A great battle was joined at the Xiyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 勒躬貫甲冑，出自閶闔門，夾擊之。

translations.literal: Le personally donned armor and emerged from the Changhe Gate to attack them from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Le himself buckled on armor, came out through the Changhe Gate, and struck them from both flanks.

sentences.zh: 曜少而嗜酒，末年尤甚；

translations.literal: Yao had loved wine since youth, and in his later years indulged all the more;
translations.idiomatic: Yao had been fond of wine since youth, and in his later years indulged all the more;

sentences.zh: 將戰，飲酒數鬥。

translations.literal: As the battle was about to begin, he drank several dou of wine.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle he drank several dou of wine.

sentences.zh: 常乘赤馬無故停頓，乃乘小馬。

translations.literal: His usual red horse for no reason stopped and stalled, so he mounted a smaller horse.
translations.idiomatic: The red horse he usually rode halted for no reason, so he switched to a smaller mount.

sentences.zh: 比出，復飲酒斗餘。

translations.literal: By the time he set out, he had drunk more than a dou again.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he rode out he had drunk more than another dou.

sentences.zh: 至西陽門，揮陳就平。

translations.literal: When he reached the Xiyang Gate, he waved his forces forward onto level ground.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xiyang Gate he waved his battle line forward onto open ground.

sentences.zh: 石堪因而乘之，趙兵大潰。

translations.literal: Shi Kan took advantage of this to press the attack, and the Zhao army collapsed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kan pressed the advantage and the Zhao army broke in complete rout.

sentences.zh: 曜昏醉退走，馬陷石渠，墜於冰上，被瘡十餘，通中者三，為堪所執。

translations.literal: Yao, drunk and dazed, retreated; his horse sank into a stone culvert and he fell onto the ice, suffering more than ten wounds, three of them piercing strikes; he was captured by Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, reeling drunk, fled; his horse foundered in a stone channel and he fell onto the ice, taking more than ten wounds, three of them deep thrusts. Kan captured him.

sentences.zh: 勒遂大破趙兵，斬首五萬餘級。

translations.literal: Le then utterly broke the Zhao army, taking more than fifty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Le then routed the Zhao army and took more than fifty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 下令曰：「所欲擒者一人耳，今已獲之。

translations.literal: He issued an order: "The one I wished to capture was a single man, and I have already got him.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "The one man I wanted to capture is already in hand.

sentences.zh: 其敕將士抑鋒止銳，縱其歸命之路。

translations.literal: Charge the generals and soldiers to restrain their edge and halt their sharpness, and leave them a path to surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Tell the officers and men to hold back their blades and give the enemy a way to surrender."

sentences.zh: 曜見勒，曰：「石王，頗憶重門之盟否？

translations.literal: When Yao saw Le, he said: "King Shi, do you still remember the covenant at Chongmen?
translations.idiomatic: When Yao saw Le, he said: "King Shi, do you still remember our covenant at Chongmen?

sentences.zh: 」勒使徐光謂之曰：「今日之事，天使其然，復雲何邪！

translations.literal: " Le had Xu Guang tell him: "Today's affair is Heaven's doing—what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: Le had Xu Guang tell him: "What has happened today is Heaven's decree. What more is there to say!

sentences.zh: 」乙酉，勒班師。

translations.literal: " On the day yiyou, Le withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Le marched his army home.

sentences.zh: 使征東將軍石邃將兵衛送曜。

translations.literal: He sent Eastern Campaign General Shi Sui to lead troops to guard and escort Yao.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Eastern Campaign General Shi Sui with troops to guard and escort Yao.

sentences.zh: 邃，虎之子也。

translations.literal: Sui was Hu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was Hu's son.

sentences.zh: 曜瘡甚，載以馬輿，使醫李永與同載。

translations.literal: Yao's wounds were severe; he was carried in a horse-litter, and the physician Li Yong was made to ride with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's wounds were grave, so he was carried in a horse-litter with the physician Li Yong riding beside him.

sentences.zh: 己亥，至襄國，捨曜於永豐小城，給其妓妾，嚴兵圍守。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, they reached Xiangguo, lodged Yao in the small city of Yongfeng, supplied him with singing girls and concubines, and surrounded him with strict troops.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai they reached Xiangguo, housed Yao in the small city of Yongfeng, gave him singing girls and concubines, and posted a tight guard around him.

sentences.zh: 遣劉岳、劉震等從男女盛服以見之，曜曰：「吾謂卿等久為灰土，石王仁厚，乃全宥至今邪！

translations.literal: He sent Liu Yue, Liu Zhen, and others, who came before him in splendid dress with their wives and children; Yao said: "I thought you had long since turned to ash and dust—King Shi is so generous and kind that he has spared you all until now!
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Yue, Liu Zhen, and others to see him, dressed in their finest with wives and children in tow. Yao said: "I thought you had long been dust. King Shi is so generous that he has spared you until now!

sentences.zh: 我殺石佗，愧之多矣。

translations.literal: I killed Shi Tuo—how much shame that brings me.
translations.idiomatic: I killed Shi Tuo, and the shame of it weighs heavily on me.

sentences.zh: 今日之禍，自其分耳。

translations.literal: Today's disaster is simply what my lot deserved.
translations.idiomatic: The disaster that has befallen me today is only what I had coming.

sentences.zh: 」留宴終日而去。

translations.literal: " He kept them feasting all day before they departed.
translations.idiomatic: He kept them at feast all day before they left.

sentences.zh: 勒使曜與其太子熙書，諭令速降；

translations.literal: Le had Yao write to his heir Xi, instructing him to surrender quickly;
translations.idiomatic: Le had Yao write to his heir Xi urging a prompt surrender;

sentences.zh: 曜但敕熙與諸大臣「匡維社稷，勿以吾易意也。

translations.literal: Yao only charged Xi and the chief ministers: "Uphold and preserve the altars of state; do not change your resolve because of me."
translations.idiomatic: Yao only told Xi and the chief ministers: "Uphold the realm and do not change your resolve because of me."

sentences.zh: 」勒見而惡之，久之，乃殺曜。

translations.literal: " When Le saw this he was displeased; after some time he had Yao killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Le read it he was displeased, and after a time he had Yao executed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，成漢獻王驤卒，其子征東將軍壽以喪還成都。

translations.literal: That year, Cheng-Han's Prince Xian Wang Xiang died; his son Eastern Campaign General Shou returned to Chengdu for the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: That year Cheng-Han's Prince Xian Wang Xiang died, and his son Eastern Campaign General Shou returned to Chengdu for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 成主雄以李玝為征北將軍、梁州刺史，代壽屯晉壽。

translations.literal: Cheng-Han's ruler Xiong appointed Li Huan Northern Campaign General and Inspector of Liang Province to replace Shou and garrison Jinshou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng-Han's ruler Xiong appointed Li Huan Northern Campaign General and Inspector of Liang Province to replace Shou and hold Jinshou.

sentences.zh: 顯宗成皇帝上之下咸和四年（

translations.literal: Lower fascicle of the reign of Emperor Cheng the Manifest Ancestor, Xianhe year 4 (
translations.idiomatic: From the lower fascicle of the reign of Emperor Cheng (Manifest Ancestor), Xianhe year 4 (

sentences.zh: 己丑、公元三二九年）

translations.literal: jichou, corresponding to 329 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jichou, corresponding to 329 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，光祿大夫陸曄及弟尚書左僕射玩說匡術，以苑城附於西軍；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Palace Attendant Lu Ye and his younger brother Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Wan persuaded Kuang Shu to submit the Garden City to the western army;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Palace Attendant Lu Ye and his younger brother Left Vice Director Lu Wan persuaded Kuang Shu to turn the Garden City over to the western army;

sentences.zh: 百官皆赴之，推曄督宮城軍事。

translations.literal: all the officials went to join them, and Ye was chosen to direct military affairs in the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: the officials all rallied to them, and Ye was chosen to direct military affairs in the palace city.

sentences.zh: 陶侃命毛寶守南城，鄧岳守西城。

translations.literal: Tao Kan ordered Mao Bao to hold the South City and Deng Yue to hold the West City.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan ordered Mao Bao to hold the South City and Deng Yue the West City.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍齊超、侍中鐘雅與建康令管旆等謀奉帝出赴西軍；

translations.literal: Right Guard General Qi Chao, Palace Attendant Zhong Ya, and Jiankang magistrate Guan Pei and others plotted to escort the emperor out to join the western army;
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard General Qi Chao, Palace Attendant Zhong Ya, Jiankang magistrate Guan Pei, and others plotted to escort the emperor out to the western army;

sentences.zh: 事洩，蘇逸使其將平原任讓將兵入宮收超、雅。

translations.literal: the affair leaked out; Su Yi had his general Ren Rang of Pingyuan lead troops into the palace to seize Chao and Ya.
translations.idiomatic: when the plot leaked, Su Yi sent his general Ren Rang of Pingyuan with troops into the palace to seize Chao and Ya.

sentences.zh: 帝抱持悲泣曰：「還我侍中、右衛！

translations.literal: The emperor clung to them, weeping in grief, and said: "Give me back my Palace Attendant and Right Guard!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor clung to them, weeping, and cried: "Give me back my Palace Attendant and Right Guard!

sentences.zh: 」讓奪而殺之。

translations.literal: " Rang tore them away and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Rang tore them free and killed them.

sentences.zh: 初，讓少無行，太常華恆為本州大中正，黜其品。

translations.literal: Earlier, Rang in youth had been without proper conduct; Grand Commandant Hua Heng, as chief arbiter of the province, lowered his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Rang had been dissolute in youth, and Grand Commandant Hua Heng, as the province's chief arbiter, lowered his rank.

sentences.zh: 及讓為蘇峻將，乘勢多所誅殺，見恆輒恭敬，不敢縱暴。

translations.literal: When Rang became one of Su Jun's generals, he used his power to execute many; yet whenever he saw Heng he was respectful and did not dare act violently.
translations.idiomatic: When Rang became one of Su Jun's generals he used his power to kill many, yet whenever he saw Heng he was respectful and did not dare act violently.

sentences.zh: 及鐘、劉之死，蘇逸欲並殺恆，讓盡心救衛，恆乃得免。

translations.literal: When Zhong and Liu died, Su Yi wished to kill Heng as well; Rang exerted himself to protect and save him, and Heng was spared.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong and Liu were killed, Su Yi wanted to kill Heng too, but Rang defended him with all his strength and Heng was spared.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍趙胤遣部將甘苗擊祖約於歷陽，戊辰，約夜帥左右數百人奔後趙，其將牽騰帥眾出降。

translations.literal: Champion General Zhao Yin sent his subordinate general Gan Miao to attack Zu Yue at Liyang; on the day wuchen, Yue led several hundred close followers by night to flee to Later Zhao, and his general Qian Teng led the host out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Champion General Zhao Yin sent his subordinate Gan Miao to attack Zu Yue at Liyang. On wuchen, Yue fled by night with several hundred close followers to Later Zhao, and his general Qian Teng led the troops out in surrender.

sentences.zh: 蘇逸、蘇碩、韓晃並力攻台城，焚太極東堂及秘閣，毛寶登城，射殺數十人。

translations.literal: Su Yi, Su Shuo, and Han Huang combined forces to attack the Terrace City, burning the eastern hall of the Grand Ultimate and the Secret Archives; Mao Bao mounted the wall and shot down several dozen men.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yi, Su Shuo, and Han Huang joined forces to assault the Terrace City, burning the eastern hall of the Grand Ultimate and the Secret Archives. Mao Bao took the wall and shot down dozens of men.

sentences.zh: 晃謂寶曰：「君名勇果，何不出鬥？

translations.literal: Huang said to Bao: "You are famed for courage and resolve—why do you not come out and fight?
translations.idiomatic: Huang called to Bao: "You are famed for courage—why not come down and fight?

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「君名健將，何不入鬥？

translations.literal: " Bao said: "You are famed as a stalwart general—why do you not come in and fight?
translations.idiomatic: Bao replied: "You are famed as a stalwart general—why not come up and fight?

sentences.zh: 」晃笑而退。

translations.literal: " Huang laughed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Huang laughed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 趙太子熙聞趙主曜被擒，大懼，與南陽王胤謀西保秦州。

translations.literal: Zhao's heir Xi, on hearing that Zhao's ruler Yao had been captured, was greatly afraid and plotted with Prince of Nanyang Yin to withdraw west and hold Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao's heir Xi heard that ruler Yao had been captured, he was terrified and plotted with Prince of Nanyang Yin to withdraw west and hold Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 尚書胡勳曰：「今雖喪君，境土尚完，將士不叛，且當並力拒之；

translations.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing Hu Xun said: "Though we have lost our ruler, the territory is still intact and the officers and soldiers have not rebelled; for the moment we should unite our strength to resist;
translations.idiomatic: Minister Hu Xun said: "We have lost our ruler, but the realm is still intact and the troops have not turned. We should stand together and resist;

sentences.zh: 力不能拒，走未晚也。

translations.literal: if our strength cannot hold, flight will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: if we cannot hold, there will still be time to flee."

sentences.zh: 」胤怒，以為沮眾，斬之，遂帥百官奔上邽，諸征鎮亦皆棄所守從之，關中大亂。

translations.literal: " Yin grew angry, took this as discouraging the host, and beheaded him; he then led the officials in flight to Shanggui, and the various campaigning garrisons likewise abandoned their posts to follow him, and Guanzhong fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was furious, called it demoralizing the troops, and had him executed. He then led the officials in flight to Shanggui; the frontier garrisons abandoned their posts to follow, and Guanzhong fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 將軍蔣英、辛恕擁眾數十萬據長安，遣使降後趙，後趙遣石生帥洛陽之眾赴之。

translations.literal: Generals Jiang Ying and Xin Shu gathered several hundred thousand men and held Chang'an; they sent envoys to surrender to Later Zhao, and Later Zhao sent Shi Sheng to lead the Luoyang host to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Jiang Ying and Xin Shu gathered several hundred thousand men and held Chang'an, sent envoys to surrender to Later Zhao, and Later Zhao sent Shi Sheng with the Luoyang army to support them.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙戌，諸軍攻石頭。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day bingxu, the various armies attacked Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingxu, the allied armies attacked Shitou.

sentences.zh: 建成長史滕含擊蘇逸，大破之。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator of Jiancheng Teng Han attacked Su Yi and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng chief administrator Teng Han attacked Su Yi and routed him.

sentences.zh: 蘇碩帥驍勇數百，渡准而戰，溫嶠擊斬之。

translations.literal: Su Shuo led several hundred fierce warriors, crossed the Huai to give battle, and was struck down and beheaded by Wen Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shuo led several hundred picked warriors across the Huai to fight and was killed by Wen Jiao.

sentences.zh: 韓晃等懼，以其眾就張健於曲阿，門隘不得出，更相蹈藉，死者萬數。

translations.literal: Han Huang and the others were afraid; they took their host to join Zhang Jian at Qu'e, but the gates were narrow and they could not get out; trampling one another in turn, the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang and the others, in fear, took their troops to join Zhang Jian at Qu'e. The gates were too narrow to pass, men trampled one another, and tens of thousands died.

sentences.zh: 西軍獲蘇逸，斬之。

translations.literal: The western army captured Su Yi and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The western army captured Su Yi and executed him.

sentences.zh: 滕含部將曹據抱帝奔溫嶠船，群臣見帝，頓首號泣請罪。

translations.literal: Teng Han's subordinate general Cao Ju carried the emperor in his arms and fled to Wen Jiao's boat; when the officials saw the emperor they kowtowed, wept aloud, and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Han's subordinate Cao Ju carried the emperor to Wen Jiao's boat. When the officials saw the emperor they kowtowed, wept, and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 殺西陽王羕，並其二子播、充、孫崧及彭城王雄。

translations.literal: They executed Prince of Xiyang Liu Ying, along with his two sons Bo and Chong, Sun Song, and Prince of Pengcheng Liu Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: They executed Prince of Xiyang Liu Ying, his two sons Bo and Chong, Sun Song, and Prince of Pengcheng Liu Xiong.

sentences.zh: 陶侃與任讓有舊，為請其死。

translations.literal: Tao Kan and Ren Rang had an old acquaintance, and he pleaded for Rang's life.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan had known Ren Rang of old and pleaded for his life.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「是殺吾侍中、右衛者，不可赦也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is the man who killed my Palace Attendant and Right Guard—he cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "This is the man who killed my Palace Attendant and Right Guard. He cannot be spared."

sentences.zh: 」乃殺之。

translations.literal: " He was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was then executed.

sentences.zh: 司徒導入石頭，令取故節，陶侃笑曰：「蘇武節似不如是。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Dao entered Shitou and ordered his old tally of office retrieved; Tao Kan laughed and said: "Su Wu's tally was not like this.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wang Dao entered Shitou and ordered his old tally retrieved. Tao Kan laughed and said: "Su Wu's tally did not look like that.

sentences.zh: 」導有慚色。

translations.literal: " Dao looked ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Dao flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 張健疑弘徽等貳於己，皆殺之，帥舟師自延陵將入吳興。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian suspected Hong Hui and the others of turning against him, killed them all, and led a fleet from Yanling intending to enter Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian suspected Hong Hui and the others of disloyalty, killed them all, and led a fleet from Yanling toward Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 乙未，揚烈將軍王允之與戰，大破之，獲男女萬餘口。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, General Who Displays Martial Prowess Wang Yunzhi fought him, routed him utterly, and captured more than ten thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, General Who Displays Martial Prowess Wang Yunzhi fought him, routed him, and took more than ten thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 健復與韓晃、馬雄等輕軍西趨故鄣，郗鑒遣軍李閎追之，及於平陵山，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Jian again joined Han Huang, Ma Xiong, and others with a light force and hurried west toward Guzhang; Xi Jian sent the officer Li Hong in pursuit, caught them at Mount Pingling, and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Jian joined Han Huang, Ma Xiong, and others with a light force and hurried west toward Guzhang. Xi Jian sent Li Hong in pursuit; at Mount Pingling he caught them and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 是時宮闕灰燼，以建平園為宮。

translations.literal: At this time the palace halls lay in ashes, and the Jianping Garden was used as the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The palace halls were in ashes, and the court made the Jianping Garden its residence.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠欲遷都豫章，三吳之豪請都會稽，二論紛紜未決。

translations.literal: Wen Jiao wished to move the capital to Yuzhang; the magnates of the Three Wu regions asked that it be moved to Kuaiji; the two proposals were disputed and no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao wanted to move the capital to Yuzhang, while the magnates of the Three Wu urged Kuaiji. The debate raged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 司徒導曰：「孫仲謀、劉玄德俱言：『建康，王者之宅。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Dao said: "Sun Zhongmou and Liu Xuande both said: 'Jiankang is the dwelling of a true king.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wang Dao said: "Sun Zhongmou and Liu Xuande both said: 'Jiankang is the dwelling of kings.

sentences.zh: 』古之帝王，不必以豐儉移都。

translations.literal: ' Ancient emperors and kings did not necessarily move their capitals because of plenty or want.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperors of old did not necessarily move their capitals for reasons of wealth or poverty.

sentences.zh: 苟務本節用，何憂凋弊！

translations.literal: If one devotes oneself to fundamentals and practices thrift, what fear is there of decline and ruin!
translations.idiomatic: If we devote ourselves to fundamentals and practice thrift, what need is there to fear ruin!

sentences.zh: 若農事不修，則樂土為墟矣。

translations.literal: If farming is not kept in order, even fertile land becomes a wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: If farming is neglected, even fertile land becomes a wasteland.

sentences.zh: 且北寇遊魂，伺我之隙，一旦示弱，竄於蠻越，求之望實，懼非良計。

translations.literal: Moreover, the northern invaders are restless spirits watching for our openings; if we suddenly show weakness and flee into the wilds of the south, judged by reputation and reality alike, I fear it is no good plan.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the northern enemy watches for our weakness. If we suddenly show fear and flee into the southern wilds, I fear that by reputation and reality alike it would be a poor plan.

sentences.zh: 今特宜鎮之以靜，群情自安。

translations.literal: For now we should above all calm the realm with steadfastness, and the people's hearts will settle of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: For now we should hold firm and keep still, and the people's hearts will settle of themselves."

sentences.zh: 」由是不復徙都。

translations.literal: " Because of this they did not move the capital again.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was not moved.

sentences.zh: 以褚翜為丹楊尹。

translations.literal: Chu Se was appointed Danyang intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Se was appointed intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時兵火之後，民物凋殘，翜收集散亡，京邑遂安。

translations.literal: At that time, after the fires of war, the people and their goods were wasted and broken; Se gathered the scattered and the lost, and the capital district was thereby restored to peace.
translations.idiomatic: After the war the people and their goods lay in ruins; Se gathered the scattered and dispossessed, and the capital was restored to order.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以湘州並荊州。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Xiang Province was merged into Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Xiang Province was merged into Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬子，論平蘇峻功，以陶侃為侍中、太尉，封長沙郡公，加都督交、廣、寧州諸軍事；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day renzi, in reckoning merit for pacifying Su Jun, Tao Kan was made Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Duke of Changsha commandery, and given additional command over all military affairs in Jiao, Guang, and Ning provinces;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renzi, rewards were given for pacifying Su Jun: Tao Kan was made Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, enfeoffed Duke of Changsha commandery, and given command over military affairs in Jiao, Guang, and Ning provinces;

sentences.zh: 郗鑒為侍中、司空、南昌縣公；

translations.literal: Xi Jian was made Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and Duke of Nanchang county;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian was made Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and Duke of Nanchang county;

sentences.zh: 溫嶠為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍、始安郡公；

translations.literal: Wen Jiao was made General of Agile Cavalry, given the same ceremonial honors as the Three Excellencies with an open office, and additionally made Regular Palace Attendant and Duke of Shian commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao was made General of Agile Cavalry with an open office and ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies, additionally Regular Palace Attendant and Duke of Shian commandery;

sentences.zh: 陸曄進爵江陵公；

translations.literal: Lu Ye was advanced in rank to Duke of Jiangling;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ye was ennobled Duke of Jiangling;

sentences.zh: 自餘賜爵侯、伯、子、男者甚眾。

translations.literal: besides these, very many were granted ranks as marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons.
translations.idiomatic: many others received ranks as marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons.

sentences.zh: 卞壼及二子□□、盱、醒彝、劉超、鐘雅、羊曼、陶瞻，皆加贈謚。

translations.literal: Bian Kun and his two sons [Zhen] and Xu, Huan Yi, Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Yang Man, and Tao Zhan were all given posthumous ennoblement and posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Kun and his two sons [Zhen] and Xu, Huan Yi, Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Yang Man, and Tao Zhan were all granted posthumous titles and honors.

sentences.zh: 路永、匡術、賈寧，皆蘇峻之黨也；

translations.literal: Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, and Jia Ning were all partisans of Su Jun;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, and Jia Ning had all been partisans of Su Jun;

sentences.zh: 峻未敗，永等去峻歸朝廷，王導欲賞以官爵。

translations.literal: before Jun was defeated, Yong and the others left Jun and returned to the court; Wang Dao wished to reward them with offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: before Jun's defeat they had left him and returned to the court, and Wang Dao wished to reward them with offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠曰：「永等皆峻之腹心，首為亂階，罪莫大焉。

translations.literal: Wen Jiao said: "Yong and the others were all Jun's trusted inner circle, the first to raise the rebellion—no crime could be greater.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao said: "Yong and the others were Jun's inner circle and the first to raise rebellion. No crime could be greater.

sentences.zh: 晚雖改悟，未足以贖前罪；

translations.literal: Though they came to their senses late, that is not enough to atone for their earlier crimes;
translations.idiomatic: Though they turned back late, that is not enough to atone for what they did;

sentences.zh: 得全首領，為幸多矣，豈可復褒寵之哉！

translations.literal: to keep their heads was already great fortune—how could they be honored and favored again!"
translations.idiomatic: to keep their heads was already great fortune. How could they be honored again!"

sentences.zh: 」導乃止。

translations.literal: " Dao then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Dao dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 陶侃以江陵偏遠，移鎮巴陵。

translations.literal: Tao Kan, finding Jiangling too remote, moved his headquarters to Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Jiangling too remote, Tao Kan moved his headquarters to Baling.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲留溫嶠輔政，嶠以王導先帝所任，固辭還籓；

translations.literal: At court deliberation they wished to retain Wen Jiao to assist in government; Jiao, on the grounds that Wang Dao had been appointed by the former emperor, firmly declined and returned to his frontier post;
translations.idiomatic: The court deliberated keeping Wen Jiao to help govern, but Jiao argued that Wang Dao had been the late emperor's appointee, firmly declined, and returned to his post on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 又以京邑荒殘，資用不給，乃留資蓄，具器用，而後旋於武昌。

translations.literal: Also, because the capital region was desolate and ruined and supplies were insufficient, he left behind stored provisions, provided furnishings and equipment, and only then returned to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Because the capital lay in ruins and supplies ran short, he left behind stores of provisions and furnished the necessary equipment before withdrawing to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 帝之出石頭也，庾亮見帝，稽顙哽咽，詔亮與大臣俱升御座。

translations.literal: When the emperor left Stone City, Yu Liang saw the emperor, bowed with forehead to the ground and wept convulsively; an edict summoned Liang and the high ministers together to ascend the imperial throne platform.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor emerged from Stone City, Yu Liang came before him, prostrated himself, and wept aloud. An edict then summoned Liang and the chief ministers to ascend the imperial seat together.

sentences.zh: 明日，亮復泥首謝罪，乞骸骨，欲闔門投竄山海。

translations.literal: The next day, Liang again presented himself with head in the dust to confess guilt, begged to resign his bones, and wished to flee with his whole household into the mountains and seas.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Liang again prostrated himself to beg forgiveness, asked to retire from office, and wished to take his entire household and flee into remote mountains and seas.

sentences.zh: 帝遣尚書、侍中手詔慰喻曰：「此社稷之難，非舅之責也。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a personal edict through the Minister of the Secretariat and the Palace Attendant to console and instruct him, saying: "This is a calamity to the state altars—it is not my uncle's fault."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a personal edict through the Minister of the Secretariat and a Palace Attendant to comfort him: "This is a crisis of the realm—not your fault, Uncle."

sentences.zh: 」亮上疏自陳：「祖約、蘇峻縱肆凶逆，罪由臣發，寸斬屠戮，不足以謝七廟之靈，塞四海之責。

translations.literal: " Liang submitted a memorial confessing in his own words: "Zu Yue and Su Jun indulged their wicked rebellion; the crime was set in motion by me. To be cut limb from limb and slaughtered would not suffice to atone before the spirits of the seven ancestral temples or to answer the reproach of all within the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: " Liang submitted a memorial of self-accusation: "Zu Yue and Su Jun ran rampant in treason—and I set it in motion. Dismemberment and execution would not atone to the spirits of the seven temples or answer the reproach of the empire."

sentences.zh: 朝廷復何理齒臣於人次，臣亦何顏自次於人理！

translations.literal: By what principle could the court again rank me among other men? By what face could I rank myself among other men according to human propriety!
translations.idiomatic: On what grounds could the court rank me among other men? And what face have I to take my place among them?

sentences.zh: 願陛下雖垂寬宥，全其首領；

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty may show clemency and spare my head and neck,
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty shows mercy and spares my life,

sentences.zh: 猶宜棄之，任其自存自沒，則天下粗知勸戒之綱矣。

translations.literal: you should still cast me aside and let me live or perish as fate wills—then the realm would at least know the guiding rope of admonition and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: you should still cast me aside and let me live or die as fate wills, so that the realm may at least learn the lesson of restraint.

sentences.zh: 」優詔不許。

translations.literal: " A gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " A gracious edict refused his request.

sentences.zh: 亮又欲遁逃山海，自暨陽東出；

translations.literal: Liang again wished to flee into the mountains and seas, leaving eastward from Jiyang;
translations.idiomatic: Liang again tried to flee into the wilds, heading east from Jiyang;

sentences.zh: 詔有司錄奪舟船。

translations.literal: an edict ordered the relevant offices to seize and confiscate boats and ships.
translations.idiomatic: and an edict ordered officials to seize his boats.

sentences.zh: 亮乃求外鎮自效，出為都督豫州、揚州之江西、宣城諸軍事、豫州刺史，領宣城內史，鎮蕪湖。

translations.literal: Liang then sought a frontier post to prove his worth, and was sent out as Commander of all military affairs in Yuzhou, Jiangxi in Yangzhou, and Xuancheng, Governor of Yuzhou, concurrently Administrator of Xuancheng, garrisoning Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then asked for a frontier command to prove his loyalty. He was appointed Commander of military affairs in Yuzhou, Jiangxi in Yangzhou, and Xuancheng; Governor of Yuzhou and concurrent Administrator of Xuancheng, with his headquarters at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 陶侃、溫嶠之討蘇峻也，移檄征、鎮，使各引兵入援。

translations.literal: When Tao Kan and Wen Jiao marched against Su Jun, they issued a proclamation to the expeditionary generals and regional commanders, ordering each to lead troops in relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan and Wen Jiao marched against Su Jun, they issued a proclamation to field armies and regional commands, summoning each to bring troops to the relief of the capital.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史益陽侯卞敦擁兵不赴，又不給軍糧，遣督護將數百人隨大軍而已，朝野莫不怪歎。

translations.literal: Bian Dun, Marquis of Yiyang and Governor of Xiangzhou, held his troops back and did not come; he also refused to supply army grain, sending only a few hundred men under a commandant-protector to follow the main army—and no one at court or in the realm did not marvel and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Dun, Marquis of Yiyang and Governor of Xiangzhou, held back his troops and neither marched nor supplied grain, sending only a few hundred men under a commandant-protector to follow the main army. Court and countryside alike marveled and sighed at this.

sentences.zh: 及峻平，陶侃奏敦阻軍，顧望不赴國難，請檻車收付廷尉。

translations.literal: When Jun was subdued, Tao Kan memorialized that Dun had obstructed the army and hung back without answering the state's crisis, requesting that he be taken in a caged cart and delivered to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun's defeat, Tao Kan memorialized that Dun had obstructed the army and hung back from the national crisis, asking that he be taken in a prison cart to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 王導以喪亂之後，宜加寬宥，轉敦安南將軍、廣州刺史；

translations.literal: Wang Dao, considering that after the mourning and turmoil leniency should be shown, transferred Dun to General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Guangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao, arguing that magnanimity was called for after the devastation, transferred Dun to General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Guangzhou;

sentences.zh: 病不赴，征為光祿大夫、領少府。

translations.literal: citing illness he did not take up the post; he was summoned as Grand Master for Glorious Merit and concurrently Prefect of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: but Dun claimed illness and did not report. He was then summoned to serve as Grand Master for Glorious Merit and Prefect of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 敦憂愧而卒，追贈本官，加散騎常侍，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: Dun died of grief and shame; posthumously he was granted his former office, was additionally made Regular Palace Attendant, and was given the posthumous name Jing ("Respectful").
translations.idiomatic: Dun died of shame and grief. Posthumously he was restored to his former rank with the additional title Regular Palace Attendant, and his posthumous name was Jing, "Respectful."

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：「庾亮以外戚輔政，首發禍機，國破君危，竄身苟免；

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: "Yu Liang, as maternal kin assisting in government, first set the calamity in motion; the state was shattered and the ruler endangered, yet he hid himself and barely escaped;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: "As an imperial in-law helping govern, Yu Liang set the catastrophe in motion; the realm was shattered and the sovereign imperiled, yet he slunk away and saved his own skin;

sentences.zh: 卞敦位列方鎮，兵糧俱足，朝廷顛覆，坐觀勝負。

translations.literal: Bian Dun held rank among the regional commands, with troops and grain both ample; when the court was overturned, he sat and watched the outcome.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Dun commanded a frontier region with ample troops and grain, yet when the throne was overturned he sat by and watched who would win.

sentences.zh: 人臣之罪，孰大於此！

translations.literal: Among the crimes of subjects, what could be greater than this!
translations.idiomatic: What crime of a subject could be greater?

sentences.zh: 既不能明正典刑，又以寵祿報之，晉室無政，亦可知矣。

translations.literal: Yet they could neither clearly enforce the regular punishments, and instead repaid them with favor and salary—and that the Jin house had no government may be known from this as well.
translations.idiomatic: The court could neither enforce the law nor bring itself to punish them, rewarding them instead with honors and stipends. That the Jin had ceased to govern is plain enough.

sentences.zh: 任是責者，豈非王導乎！

translations.literal: He who bears this responsibility—is it not Wang Dao!
translations.idiomatic: And who bears responsibility for this? Surely Wang Dao!

sentences.zh: 徙高密王紘為彭城王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gaomi, Hong, was moved to be Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gaomi, Hong, was transferred to be Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 紘，雄之弟也。

translations.literal: Hong was the younger brother of Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was the younger brother of Xiong.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙未，始安忠武公溫嶠卒，葬於豫章。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day yimwei, Wen Jiao, Duke of Shian with the posthumous epithet Zhongwu, died and was buried at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day yimwei, Wen Jiao, posthumously Duke Zhongwu of Shian, died and was buried at Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲為之造大墓於元、明二帝陵之北，太尉侃上表曰：「嶠忠誠著於聖世，勳義感於人神。

translations.literal: The court wished to build a great tomb for him north of the tombs of Emperors Yuan and Ming; Grand Commandant Kan submitted a memorial saying: "Jiao's loyalty was manifest in the sacred age, and his meritorious righteousness moved both men and spirits."
translations.idiomatic: The court proposed building a grand tomb for him north of the tombs of Emperors Yuan and Ming. Grand Commandant Tao Kan memorialized: "Jiao's loyalty was manifest in this sacred age, and his deeds moved both men and spirits."

sentences.zh: 使亡而有知，豈樂今日勞費之事！

translations.literal: If the dead have knowledge, how could he take pleasure in today's toil and expense!
translations.idiomatic: If the dead retain any awareness, how could he delight in such expense and labor today!

sentences.zh: 願陛下慈恩，停其移葬。

translations.literal: I beseech Your Majesty's compassionate grace to halt the transfer of his burial.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty's merciful grace to halt the plan to move his grave.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 以平南軍司劉胤為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Yin, Chief of Staff of the Army That Pacifies the South, was made Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, chief of staff to the Army That Pacifies the South, was appointed Governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 陶侃、郗鑒皆言胤非方伯才，司徒導不從。

translations.literal: Tao Kan and Chi Jian both said that Yin was not talented enough for a regional commander; Minister of Education Dao did not follow their advice.
translations.idiomatic: Both Tao Kan and Chi Jian argued that Yin lacked the talent for a regional command, but Minister of Education Wang Dao would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 或謂導子悅曰：「今大難之後，紀綱弛頓。

translations.literal: Someone said to Dao's son Yue: "Now after the great calamity, law and order are lax and slack."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Wang Dao's son Yue: "After the great crisis, discipline has grown slack throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 自江陵至於建康三千餘里，流民萬計，布在江州。

translations.literal: From Jiangling to Jiankang is more than three thousand li, and displaced persons number in the tens of thousands, spread across Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiangling to Jiankang stretches more than three thousand li, and tens of thousands of displaced people are scattered across Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 江州，國之南籓，要害之地，而胤以□侈之性，臥而對之，不有外變，必有內患矣。

translations.literal: Jiangzhou is the southern bulwark of the state, a place of vital importance; yet Yin, by nature extravagant and overbearing, lies idle over it—if no external crisis arises, there will surely be internal trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou is the dynasty's southern shield, yet Liu Yin, vain and domineering, lounges over it; even without foreign attack, trouble will brew within.

sentences.zh: 」悅曰：「此溫平南之意也。

translations.literal: " Yue said: "This is the intention of Wen, Pacifier of the South."
translations.idiomatic: " Yue replied: "That reflects Wen Jiao's view."

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，趙南陽王胤帥眾數萬自上邽趣長安，隴東、武都、安定、新平、北地、扶風、始平諸郡戎、夏皆起兵應之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Yin, Prince of Nanyang of Zhao, led a host of tens of thousands from Shanggui toward Chang'an; the Rong and Xia peoples of Longdong, Wudu, Anding, Xinping, Beidi, Fufeng, and Shiping and other commanderies all raised troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, Zhao's Prince of Nanyang, Yin, led tens of thousands of men from Shanggui toward Chang'an. The tribal peoples of Longdong, Wudu, Anding, Xinping, Beidi, Fufeng, Shiping, and other commanderies all rose in support.

sentences.zh: 胤軍於仲橋；

translations.literal: Yin encamped his army at Zhongqiao;
translations.idiomatic: Yin encamped at Zhongqiao;

sentences.zh: 石生嬰城自守，後趙中山公虎帥騎二萬救之。

translations.literal: Shi Sheng closed the city gates and defended himself; Hu, Duke of Zhongshan of Later Zhao, led twenty thousand horsemen to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng barricaded himself in the city, and Hu, Duke of Zhongshan of Later Zhao, led twenty thousand cavalry to his relief.

sentences.zh: 九月，虎大破趙兵於義渠，胤奔還上邽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Hu utterly defeated the Zhao army at Yiqu; Yin fled back to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Hu routed the Zhao army at Yiqu, and Yin fled back to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 虎乘勝追擊，枕屍千里。

translations.literal: Hu pressed the victory in pursuit; corpses lay piled for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Hu pressed the pursuit, and corpses lay piled for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 上邽潰，虎執趙太子熙、南陽王胤及其將王公卿校以下三千餘人，皆殺之，徙其台省文武、關東流民、秦雍大族九千餘人於襄國；

translations.literal: Shanggui fell; Hu seized Zhao's crown prince Xi, Prince of Nanyang Yin, and their generals, kings, dukes, ministers, and officers down to the rank of commandant—more than three thousand men in all—and put them all to death; he moved more than nine thousand civil and military officials of the court, displaced persons from east of the Pass, and great clans of Qin and Yong to Xiangguo;
translations.idiomatic: When Shanggui fell, Hu seized Zhao's crown prince Xi, Prince of Nanyang Yin, and more than three thousand of their commanders and officials down to the rank of commandant, and put them all to death. He then relocated more than nine thousand court officials, displaced people from east of the Pass, and great clans of Qin and Yong to Xiangguo;

sentences.zh: 又坑五郡屠各五千餘人於洛陽。

translations.literal: he also buried alive more than five thousand Tuge of five commanderies at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: and at Luoyang buried alive more than five thousand Tuge tribesmen from five commanderies.

sentences.zh: 進攻集木且羌於河西，克之，俘獲數萬，秦、隴悉平。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack the Jimumu Qiang west of the river, took them, captured tens of thousands, and Qin and Long were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked the Jimumu Qiang west of the Yellow River, defeated them, and took tens of thousands captive. Qin and Long were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 氐王蒲洪、羌酋姚戈仲俱降於虎，虎表洪監六夷軍事，弋仲為六夷左都督。

translations.literal: The Di king Pu Hong and the Qiang chieftain Yao Yizhong both surrendered to Hu; Hu memorialized that Hong should oversee the military affairs of the Six Yi, and Yizhong should be Left Commander of the Six Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Di king Pu Hong and the Qiang chieftain Yao Yizhong both surrendered to Hu. Hu memorialized that Hong should oversee the military affairs of the Six Yi peoples, with Yizhong as Left Commander of the Six Yi.

sentences.zh: 徙氐、羌十五萬落於司、冀州。

translations.literal: He moved one hundred fifty thousand Di and Qiang households to Sizhou and Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated one hundred fifty thousand Di and Qiang households to Sizhou and Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，隴西鮮卑乞伏述延居於苑川，侵並鄰部，士馬強盛。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qifu Shuyan of the Longxi Xianbei dwelt at Yuanchuan, encroached upon and annexed neighboring tribes, and his warriors and horses were strong and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qifu Shuyan of the Longxi Xianbei had settled at Yuanchuan, encroaching on neighboring tribes until his warriors and horses grew strong and numerous.

sentences.zh: 及趙亡，述延懼，遷於麥田。

translations.literal: When Zhao perished, Shuyan was afraid and moved to Maitian.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao fell, Shuyan grew fearful and moved his people to Maitian.

sentences.zh: 述延卒，子辱大寒立；

translations.literal: Shuyan died, and his son Ruhán Dàhán succeeded him;
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan died, and his son Ruhán Dàhán succeeded him;

sentences.zh: 辱大寒立；

translations.literal: Ruhán Dàhán succeeded;
translations.idiomatic: Ruhán Dàhán succeeded;

sentences.zh: 大寒卒，子司繁立。

translations.literal: Dàhán died, and his son Sifan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Dàhán died, and his son Sifan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史劉胤矜豪日甚，專務商販，殖財百萬，縱酒耽樂，不恤政事。

translations.literal: Liu Yin, Governor of Jiangzhou, grew daily more arrogant and proud; he devoted himself to trade, amassed wealth in the millions, indulged in wine and pleasure, and gave no thought to government.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, Governor of Jiangzhou, grew ever more arrogant. He devoted himself to commerce, amassed a fortune in the millions, and drowned himself in wine and pleasure while neglecting his duties.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，詔征後將軍郭默為右軍將軍。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, an edict summoned Rear General Guo Mo to be General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, an edict summoned Rear General Guo Mo to serve as General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 默樂為邊將，不願宿衛，以情訴於胤。

translations.literal: Mo was pleased to serve as a frontier general and did not wish to guard the palace; he appealed to Yin on personal grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Mo preferred frontier command to palace guard duty and appealed to Yin on personal grounds.

sentences.zh: 胤曰：「此非小人之所及也。

translations.literal: Yin said: "This is not something within a petty man's reach."
translations.idiomatic: Yin replied: "That is not for a petty man like me to decide."

sentences.zh: 」默將赴召，求資於胤，胤不與，默由是怨胤。

translations.literal: " As Mo was about to answer the summons, he asked Yin for supplies; Yin would not give them, and from this Mo resented Yin.
translations.idiomatic: " As Mo prepared to answer the summons, he asked Yin for supplies. Yin refused, and Mo came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 胤長史張滿等素輕默，或裸露見之，默常切齒。

translations.literal: Yin's chief clerk Zhang Man and others had long looked down on Mo; sometimes they received him while half naked, and Mo often gnashed his teeth in rage.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's chief clerk Zhang Man and others had long looked down on Mo, sometimes receiving him while half dressed, and Mo gnashed his teeth in fury.

sentences.zh: 臘日，胤餉默豚酒，默對信投之水中。

translations.literal: On the La festival day, Yin sent Mo pork and wine; Mo, in the presence of the messenger, threw them into the water.
translations.idiomatic: On the La festival day Yin sent Mo pork and wine; Mo threw them into the water before the messenger.

sentences.zh: 會有司奏：「今朝廷空竭，百官無祿，惟資江州運漕，而胤商旅繼路，以私廢公，請免胤官。

translations.literal: At this time the relevant offices memorialized: "Now the court is empty and exhausted, and the hundred officials have no salaries; it relies solely on Jiangzhou's transport of grain—and yet Yin has merchants and travelers crowding the roads, putting private gain before public duty. We ask that Yin be removed from office."
translations.idiomatic: Just then the relevant offices memorialized: "The court is bankrupt and officials go unpaid, relying solely on grain shipped from Jiangzhou—yet Yin fills the roads with his private trade, putting personal profit before public duty. We ask that he be removed from office."

sentences.zh: 」書下，胤不即歸罪，方自申理。

translations.literal: " When the document was issued, Yin did not at once accept guilt but was still pleading his own case.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, Yin did not accept blame at once but set about defending himself.

sentences.zh: 僑人蓋肫掠人女為妻，張滿使還其家，肫不從，而謂郭默曰：「劉江州不受免，密有異圖，與張滿等日夜計議，惟忌郭侯一人，欲先除之。

translations.literal: Gai Tun, a displaced person, had seized another man's daughter as his wife; Zhang Man ordered her returned to her family, but Tun would not obey and said to Guo Mo: "Governor Liu of Jiangzhou has not accepted dismissal and secretly harbors a different design; with Zhang Man and others he plots day and night, fearing only Lord Guo and wishing to eliminate him first."
translations.idiomatic: Gai Tun, a displaced man, had abducted a woman as his wife. Zhang Man ordered her returned to her family, but Tun refused and told Guo Mo: "Governor Liu has not accepted dismissal and secretly plots rebellion. He and Zhang Man scheme day and night, fearing only you, Lord Guo—they mean to kill you first."

sentences.zh: 」默以為然，帥其徒候旦門開襲胤。

translations.literal: " Mo believed this, led his followers to wait until dawn when the gate opened, and attacked Yin.
translations.idiomatic: " Mo believed him, led his followers to wait until dawn when the gate opened, and attacked Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤將吏欲拒默，默呵之曰：「我被詔有所討，動者誅三族！

translations.literal: Yin's generals and officials wished to resist Mo; Mo shouted at them: "I have received an edict to carry out a punitive mission—whoever moves, his three clans shall be executed!"
translations.idiomatic: Yin's officers tried to resist, but Mo shouted: "I act under imperial orders—move, and your three clans die!"

sentences.zh: 」遂入至內寢，牽胤下，斬之；

translations.literal: " He then entered to the inner sleeping chamber, dragged Yin down, and beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: " He entered the inner chamber, dragged Yin down, and beheaded him;

sentences.zh: 出，取胤僚佐張滿等，誣以大逆，悉斬之。

translations.literal: going out, he seized Yin's aides Zhang Man and others, falsely charged them with great treason, and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Then he seized Yin's aides Zhang Man and others, falsely charged them with treason, and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 傳胤首於京師，詐作詔書，宣示內外。

translations.literal: He sent Yin's head to the capital, forged an edict, and proclaimed it within and without.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yin's head to the capital, forged an edict, and proclaimed it throughout the court and realm.

sentences.zh: 掠胤女及諸妾並金寶還船，初雲下都，既而停胤故府。

translations.literal: He plundered Yin's daughter and concubines along with gold and jewels and returned to his boat; at first he said he would go down to the capital, but then he stopped at Yin's former residence.
translations.idiomatic: He plundered Yin's daughter and concubines along with gold and jewels and returned to his boat. At first he claimed he would sail to the capital, but instead he stayed at Yin's former residence.

sentences.zh: 招引譙國內史桓宣，宣固守不從。

translations.literal: He tried to win over Huan Xuan, Administrator of Qiaoguo, but Xuan held firm and would not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to win over Huan Xuan, administrator of Qiaoguo, but Xuan held firm and refused.

sentences.zh: 是歲，賀蘭部及諸大人共立拓跋翳槐為代王，代王紇那奔宇文部。

translations.literal: That year, the Helan tribe and the various chieftains jointly installed Tuoba Yihuai as Prince of Dai; the Prince of Dai Henà fled to the Yuwen tribe.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Helan tribe and other chieftains jointly installed Tuoba Yihuai as Prince of Dai, while the former Prince of Dai, Henà, fled to the Yuwen tribe.

sentences.zh: 翳槐遣其弟什翼犍質於趙以請和。

translations.literal: Yihuai sent his younger brother Shiyijian as hostage to Zhao to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yihuai sent his younger brother Shiyijian to Zhao as a hostage to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 河南王吐延，雄勇多猜忌，羌酋姜聰刺之；

translations.literal: Tuyan, King of Henan, was brave and fierce but much given to suspicion; the Qiang chieftain Jiang Cong assassinated him;
translations.idiomatic: Tuyan, King of Henan, was brave but deeply suspicious; the Qiang chieftain Jiang Cong assassinated him;

sentences.zh: 吐延不抽劍，召其將紇扢泥，使輔其子葉延，保於白蘭，抽劍而死。

translations.literal: Tuyan did not draw his sword; he summoned his general Hegeni, had him assist his son Yeyan and protect him at Bailan, then drew his sword and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyan did not draw his sword. He summoned his general Hegeni, entrusted his son Yeyan to him, and had them withdraw to Bailan; then he drew his sword and died.

sentences.zh: 葉延孝而好學，以為禮「公孫之子得以王父字為氏」，乃自號其國曰吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Yeyan was filial and fond of learning; he considered that ritual says "the son of a duke's son may take his grandfather's style as his clan name," and so styled his state Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Yeyan was filial and studious. Citing the rite that "a grandson may take his grandfather's style as his clan name," he named his state Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 顯宗成皇帝上之下咸和五年（

translations.literal: Lower fascicle of the reign of Emperor Cheng the Manifest Ancestor, Xianhe year 5 (
translations.idiomatic: From the lower fascicle of the reign of Emperor Cheng (Manifest Ancestor), Xianhe year 5 (

sentences.zh: 庚寅，公元三三零年）

translations.literal: gengyin, corresponding to 330 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengyin, corresponding to 330 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，劉胤首至建康。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Liu Yin's head reached Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Liu Yin's head arrived at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 司徒導以郭默驍勇難制，己亥，大赦，梟胤首於大航，以默為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Dao, considering Guo Mo fierce and brave and hard to control, on the day jihai proclaimed a general amnesty, displayed Yin's head at the Great Pontoon Bridge, and made Mo Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Wang Dao, deeming Guo Mo too fierce and unruly to control, proclaimed a general amnesty on the day jihai, displayed Yin's head at the Great Pontoon Bridge, and appointed Mo Governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 太尉侃聞之，投袂起曰：「此必詐也。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Kan heard of it, threw down his sleeves and rose, saying: "This must be a fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Tao Kan heard the news, threw down his sleeves, and declared: "This must be a fraud."

sentences.zh: 」即將兵討之。

translations.literal: " He immediately raised troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately marched to punish Mo.

sentences.zh: 默遣使送妓妾及絹，並寫中詔呈侃。

translations.literal: Mo sent envoys bearing singing girls, concubines, and silk, and also copied out the secret edict to present to Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Mo sent envoys with singing girls, concubines, and silk, and copied out the secret edict for Kan.

sentences.zh: 參佐多諫曰：「默不被詔，豈敢為此！

translations.literal: Many of his aides remonstrated, saying: "If Mo had not received an edict, how would he dare do this!"
translations.idiomatic: Many of his staff urged caution: "Without an imperial edict, how would Mo dare do such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 若欲進軍，宜待詔報。

translations.literal: If you wish to advance, you should wait for an edict in reply.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to march, you should wait for orders from the capital.

sentences.zh: 」侃厲色曰：「國家年幼，詔令不出胸懷。

translations.literal: " Kan said sternly: "The state is young, and edicts do not issue from one's own breast."
translations.idiomatic: " Kan said sternly: "The throne is still young—edicts do not issue from a man's own breast."

sentences.zh: 劉胤為朝廷所禮，雖方任非才，何緣猥加極刑！

translations.literal: Liu Yin was honored by the court; though his regional appointment was beyond his talent, by what cause was he so basely subjected to extreme punishment!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin was a man the court honored. Even if his appointment exceeded his talents, what justified so brutal a death!

sentences.zh: 郭默恃勇，所在貪暴；

translations.literal: Guo Mo relies on his courage and wherever he goes is greedy and violent;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo trusts in his courage and wherever he goes is greedy and violent;

sentences.zh: 以大難新除，禁網寬簡，欲因際會騁其從橫耳！

translations.literal: with the great calamity just ended and the prohibitions lax and simple, he wishes to seize the moment and give free rein to his wilfulness!
translations.idiomatic: With the great crisis just past and the law still slack, he means to seize the moment and run wild!

sentences.zh: 」發使上表言狀，且與導書曰：「郭默殺方州即用為方州，害宰相便為宰相乎？

translations.literal: " He sent envoys to submit a memorial stating the facts, and wrote to Dao as well, saying: "Guo Mo kills a regional governor and is at once made regional governor—kill a chancellor and he becomes chancellor too?"
translations.idiomatic: " He dispatched envoys to memorialized the facts and wrote Wang Dao: "Guo Mo kills a regional governor and is made regional governor at once—kill a chancellor and he becomes chancellor too?"

sentences.zh: 」導乃收胤首，答侃書曰：「默據上流之勢，加有船艦成資，故苞含隱忍，使有其地，朝廷得以潛嚴；

translations.literal: " Dao then had Yin's head taken down and replied to Kan in a letter: "Mo holds the advantage of the upper reaches, and moreover has boats and ships fully equipped; therefore I forbear and swallow the humiliation, letting him keep his territory so that the court may quietly make ready;
translations.idiomatic: " Dao then had Yin's head removed and replied: "Mo holds the upper Yangzi and commands a full fleet, so I forbear and swallow the insult, letting him keep his post while the court quietly prepares;

sentences.zh: 俟足下軍到，風發相赴，豈非遵養時晦以定大事者邪！

translations.literal: when your army arrives, we shall rise with the wind and join you—is this not biding one's time in concealment to settle the great affair!"
translations.idiomatic: when your army arrives we shall rise together—is this not the way to bide one's time and settle the great matter at last?"

sentences.zh: 」侃笑曰：「是乃遵養時賊也！

translations.literal: " Kan laughed and said: "That is biding one's time to nourish the thief!"
translations.idiomatic: " Tao Kan laughed: "That is biding one's time to nourish the thief!"

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史庾亮亦請討默。

translations.literal: Yu Liang, Governor of Yuzhou, also asked to punish Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang, Governor of Yuzhou, also asked to punish Mo.

sentences.zh: 詔加亮征討都督，帥步騎二萬往與侃會。

translations.literal: An edict added to Liang the title Commander for Punitive Campaigns, and he led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to join Kan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Liang Commander for Punitive Campaigns, and he led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to join Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 西陽太守鄧岳、武昌太守劉詡皆疑桓宣與默同。

translations.literal: Deng Yue, Administrator of Xiyang, and Liu Xu, Administrator of Wuchang, both suspected that Huan Xuan was in league with Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue, administrator of Xiyang, and Liu Xu, administrator of Wuchang, both suspected Huan Xuan of colluding with Mo.

sentences.zh: 豫州西曹王隨曰：「宣尚不附祖約，豈肯同郭默邪！

translations.literal: Wang Sui of the Western Bureau of Yuzhou said: "Xuan would not even follow Zu Yue—how could he join Guo Mo!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui of the Western Bureau of Yuzhou said: "Xuan would not even side with Zu Yue—how could he join Guo Mo!"

sentences.zh: 」岳、詡遣隨詣宣觀之，隨說宣曰：「明府心雖不爾，無以自明，惟有以賢子付隨耳！

translations.literal: " Yue and Xu sent Sui to visit Xuan and observe him; Sui said to Xuan: "Your Excellency's heart may not be so, but you have no way to prove it—only by entrusting your worthy son to me!"
translations.idiomatic: " Yue and Xu sent Sui to observe Xuan. Sui told him: "Your heart may be clear, but you cannot prove it—only by entrusting your worthy son to me."

sentences.zh: 」宣乃遣其子戎與隨俱迎陶侃。

translations.literal: " Xuan then sent his son Rong with Sui together to welcome Tao Kan.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan sent his son Rong with Sui to welcome Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 侃辟戎為手彖，上宣為武昌太守。

translations.literal: Kan recruited Rong as a personal aide and memorialized Xuan as Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan enrolled Huan Rong as aide and memorialized Huan Xuan as administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 二月，後趙群臣請後趙王勒即皇帝位；

translations.literal: In the second month, the ministers of Later Zhao requested that Later Zhao King Shi Le assume the title of emperor;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the ministers of Later Zhao asked King Shi Le of Later Zhao to ascend the imperial throne;

sentences.zh: 勒乃稱大趙天王，行皇帝事。

translations.literal: Le thereupon styled himself Heavenly King of Great Zhao and exercised the affairs of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le styled himself Heavenly King of Great Zhao and acted as emperor in all but name.

sentences.zh: 立妃劉氏為王后，世子弘為太子。

translations.literal: He established Consort Liu as queen and his heir Hong as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He made Consort Liu queen and heir apparent Hong crown prince.

sentences.zh: 以其子宏為驃騎大將軍、都督中外諸軍事、大單于，封秦王；

translations.literal: He made his son Hong General of Rapid Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of all armies within and without, Grand Chanyu, and enfeoffed him as King of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his son Hong Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, supreme commander of all military affairs, and Grand Chanyu, enfeoffing him as King of Qin;

sentences.zh: 斌為左衛將軍，封太原王；

translations.literal: Bin was made General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as King of Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Bin became General of the Left Guard and was enfeoffed as King of Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 恢為輔國將軍，封南陽王。

translations.literal: Hui was made General Who Supports the State and enfeoffed as King of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was made Supporting-the-State General and enfeoffed as King of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 以中山公虎為太尉、尚書令，進爵為王；

translations.literal: He made Duke of Zhongshan Hu Grand Commandant and Director of the Masters of Writing, advancing his rank to king;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Duke of Zhongshan Shi Hu Grand Commandant and Director of the Masters of Writing, promoting him to king;

sentences.zh: 虎子邃為冀州刺史，封齊王；

translations.literal: Hu's son Sui was made Inspector of Ji Province and enfeoffed as King of Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Hu's son Sui was made governor of Ji Province and enfeoffed as King of Qi;

sentences.zh: 宣為左將軍；

translations.literal: Xuan was made General of the Left;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was made Left General;

sentences.zh: 挺為侍中，封梁王。

translations.literal: Ting was made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 又封石生為河東王，石堪為彭城王。

translations.literal: He further enfeoffed Shi Sheng as King of Hedong and Shi Kan as King of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also enfeoffed Shi Sheng as King of Hedong and Shi Kan as King of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 以左長史郭敖為尚書左僕射，右長史程遐為右僕射、領吏部尚書，左司馬夔安、右司馬郭殷、從事中郎李鳳、前郎中令裴憲，皆為尚書，參軍事徐光為中書令、領秘書監。

translations.literal: He made Left Chief Clerk Guo Ao Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Right Chief Clerk Cheng Xia Right Vice Director and concurrent Director of the Bureau of Personnel, Left Major Kui An, Right Major Guo Yin, Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Feng, and former Director of Palace Attendants Pei Xian all Masters of Writing; Military Adviser Xu Guang was made Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He made Left Chief Clerk Guo Ao Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Right Chief Clerk Cheng Xia Right Vice Director and concurrent Minister of Personnel; Left Major Kui An, Right Major Guo Yin, Attendant Li Feng, and former Palace Attendant Director Pei Xian all ministers of writing; and military adviser Xu Guang Director of the Secretariat with concurrent supervision of the Secretariat archives.

sentences.zh: 自餘文武，封拜各有差。

translations.literal: As for the remaining civil and military officials, enfeoffments and appointments each differed in degree.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining civil and military officials received titles and appointments according to their rank.

sentences.zh: 中山王虎怒，私謂齊王邃曰：「主上自都襄國以來，端拱仰成，以吾身當矢石，二十餘年，南擒劉岳，北走索頭，東平齊、魯，西定秦、雍，克十有三州。

translations.literal: King of Zhongshan Hu grew angry and said privately to King of Qi Sui: "Since the Lord above established his capital at Xiangguo, he has sat upright with folded hands and received the accomplishment—while I myself have met arrows and stones. For more than twenty years I captured Liu Yue in the south, drove off Suotou in the north, pacified Qi and Lu in the east, settled Qin and Yong in the west, and seized thirteen provinces in all.
translations.idiomatic: King of Zhongshan Shi Hu, furious, spoke privately to King of Qi Sui: "Since our lord established his capital at Xiangguo, he has sat back while I took the arrows and stones. For more than twenty years I captured Liu Yue in the south, routed the Suotou in the north, pacified Qi and Lu in the east, and settled Qin and Yong in the west—thirteen provinces in all.

sentences.zh: 成大趙之業者，我也；

translations.literal: The one who accomplished the enterprise of Great Zhao was I;
translations.idiomatic: I am the one who built Great Zhao;

sentences.zh: 大單于當以授我，今乃以與黃吻婢兒，念之令人氣塞，不能寢食！

translations.literal: The title of Grand Chanyu ought to have been given to me; now it has been given instead to a yellow-beaked boy, and to think of it makes one choke with rage and unable to sleep or eat!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Chanyu title should have gone to me, yet it was given to a beardless boy—it makes my blood boil; I cannot eat or sleep!

sentences.zh: 待主上晏駕之後，不足復留種也。

translations.literal: When we wait until after the Lord above's death, they are not worth leaving even a seed behind.
translations.idiomatic: When our lord passes away, they will not be worth leaving alive at all.

sentences.zh: 程遐言於勒曰：「天下粗定，當顯明逆順，故漢高祖赦季布，斬丁公。

translations.literal: Cheng Xia spoke to Le, saying: "The realm is roughly settled; we ought to make clear what is rebellion and what is loyalty. Hence Emperor Gaozu of Han pardoned Ji Bu and executed Duke Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xia said to Shi Le: "The realm is nearly settled, and we ought to show plainly what is loyal and what is treasonous. That is why Emperor Gaozu of Han pardoned Ji Bu and executed Duke Ding.

sentences.zh: 大王自起兵以來，見忠於其君者輒褒之，背叛不臣者輒誅之，此天下所以歸盛德也。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty raised arms, whenever you saw one loyal to his lord you at once rewarded him, and whenever you saw one who rebelled and would not serve you you at once executed him—this is why the realm submits to your lofty virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Since you took up arms, you have always rewarded loyalty and punished treason. That is why the realm has rallied to your great virtue.

sentences.zh: 今祖約猶存，臣竊惑之。

translations.literal: Now Zu Yue still lives—your servant is secretly puzzled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zu Yue still lives, and I am puzzled.

sentences.zh: 」安西將軍姚弋仲亦以為言。

translations.literal: " The General Who Pacifies the West Yao Yizhong also spoke likewise.
translations.idiomatic: " General Who Pacifies the West Yao Yizhong said the same.

sentences.zh: 勒乃收約，並其親屬中外百餘人悉誅之，妻妾兒女分賜諸胡。

translations.literal: Le thereupon arrested Yue and, together with more than a hundred of his kinsmen inside and outside, executed them all; his wives, concubines, sons, and daughters were distributed and bestowed on the various barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le then seized Zu Yue and executed him along with more than a hundred relatives and associates; his wives, concubines, and children were distributed among the various tribes.

sentences.zh: 初，祖逖有胡奴曰王安，逖甚愛之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zu Ti had a barbarian slave named Wang An, whom Ti greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zu Ti had a barbarian bondservant named Wang An whom he greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 在雍丘，謂安曰：「石勒是汝種類，吾亦無在爾一人。

translations.literal: At Yongqiu he said to An: "Shi Le is of your kind; I have no reason to keep you alone here either.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongqiu he told Wang An: "Shi Le is of your people, and I have no need to keep you here alone.

sentences.zh: 」厚資送而遣之。

translations.literal: " He gave him generous resources, sent him off, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave Wang An generous provisions and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 安以勇干，仕趙，為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: An, by reason of his courage and ability, entered the service of Zhao and was made General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang An, known for courage and ability, entered Zhao service and became General of the Left Guard.
