sentences.zh: 及約之誅，安歎曰：「豈可使祖土稚無後乎？

translations.literal: When Yue was executed, An sighed and said: "How can I allow Zu Tuzhi to have no descendants?
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Yue was executed, Wang An sighed: "How can I let Zu Tuzhi die without heirs?

sentences.zh: 」乃往就市觀刑。

translations.literal: " He then went to the marketplace to witness the execution.
translations.idiomatic: " He went to the marketplace to watch the execution.

sentences.zh: 逖庶子道重，始十歲，安竊取以歸，匿之，變服為沙門。

translations.literal: Ti's concubine-born son Daozhong, just ten years old, An secretly took and returned home, hiding him and changing his dress to that of a Buddhist monk.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti's bastard son Daozhong was only ten. Wang An stole him away, hid him, and disguised him as a Buddhist monk.

sentences.zh: 及石氏亡，道重複歸江南。

translations.literal: When the Shi clan perished, Daozhong again returned to the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shi regime fell, Daozhong returned to the south.

sentences.zh: 郭默欲南據豫章，會太尉侃兵至，默出戰，不利，入城固守，聚米為壘，以示有餘。

translations.literal: Guo Mo wished to hold Yuzhang in the south; when Grand Commandant Kan's troops arrived, Mo went out to battle, fared badly, entered the city and held fast, piled rice to make ramparts, and thereby showed that he had surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo tried to hold Yuzhang in the south, but when Grand Commandant Tao Kan's army arrived he gave battle, was defeated, retreated into the city, and piled rice into ramparts to feign abundance.

sentences.zh: 侃築土山臨之。

translations.literal: Kan built earthen mounds overlooking it.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan built siege mounds overlooking the city.

sentences.zh: 三月，庾亮兵至湓口，諸軍大集。

translations.literal: In the third month, Yu Liang's troops reached Pukou and the various armies gathered in force.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Yu Liang's forces reached Pukou and the allied armies massed.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，乙卯，默將宋侯縛默父子出降。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on yimao, Mo's general Song Hou bound Mo and his son and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on yimao, Guo Mo's general Song Hou bound Mo and his son and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 侃斬默於軍門，傳首建康，同黨死者四十人。

translations.literal: Kan executed Mo at the army gate, sent his head to Jiankang, and forty fellow conspirators died.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan executed Guo Mo at the camp gate, sent his head to Jiankang, and forty accomplices were put to death.

sentences.zh: 詔以侃都督江州，領刺史；

translations.literal: An edict made Kan Commander of Jiang Province and concurrent Inspector;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Tao Kan commander of Jiang Province and concurrent provincial governor;

sentences.zh: 以鄧岳督交、廣諸軍事，領廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Deng Yue was made overseer of military affairs in Jiao and Guang and concurrent Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue was made overseer of military affairs in Jiao and Guang and governor of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 侃還巴陵，因移鎮武昌。

translations.literal: Kan returned to Baling and thereafter moved his headquarters to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan returned to Baling and then transferred his headquarters to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 庾亮還蕪湖，辭爵賞不受。

translations.literal: Yu Liang returned to Wuhu and declined titles and rewards, refusing to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang returned to Wuhu and declined all titles and rewards.

sentences.zh: 趙將劉征帥眾數千，浮海抄東南諸縣，殺南沙都尉許儒。

translations.literal: Zhao general Liu Zheng led several thousand men, crossed the sea by boat to raid the counties of the southeast, and killed Commander of Nansha Xu Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao general Liu Zheng led several thousand men by sea to raid southeastern counties and killed Nansha commandant Xu Ru.

sentences.zh: 張駿因前趙之亡，復收河南地，至於狄道，置五屯護軍，與趙分境。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, taking advantage of Former Zhao's fall, again recovered the lands of Henan as far as Didao, established five agricultural-colony protectors, and divided the border with Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun exploited Former Zhao's collapse to recover Henan as far as Didao, established five colony-protectorates, and drew a border with Zhao.

sentences.zh: 六月，趙遣鴻臚孟毅拜駿征西大將軍、涼州牧，加九錫。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zhao sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Meng Yi to invest Jun as General Who Conquers the West and Governor of Liang Province, adding the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhao sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Meng Yi to invest Zhang Jun as General Who Conquers the West and Governor of Liang Province with the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 駿恥為之臣，不受，留毅不遣。

translations.literal: Jun was ashamed to become his subject, did not accept, and detained Yi without sending him back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was ashamed to submit and refused; he kept Meng Yi and would not send him back.

sentences.zh: 初，丁零翟斌，世居康居，後徙中國，至是入朝於趙；

translations.literal: Earlier, Dingling Zhai Bin's family had long lived in Kangju, then moved to China; at this time he came to court to Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Dingling chieftain Zhai Bin's clan had lived in Kangju before migrating to China; now he came to pay court to Zhao;

sentences.zh: 趙以斌為句町王。

translations.literal: Zhao made Bin King of Gouding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao enfeoffed Zhai Bin as King of Gouding.

sentences.zh: 趙群臣固請正尊號，秋，九月，趙王勒即皇帝位。

translations.literal: The ministers of Zhao repeatedly requested that he assume the correct exalted title; in autumn, the ninth month, Zhao King Le assumed the title of emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's ministers repeatedly urged Shi Le to take the full imperial title; in autumn, the ninth month, King Shi Le ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元建平。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the era name Jianping.

sentences.zh: 文武封進各有差。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials received advancement in enfeoffment each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials received promotions and titles according to merit.

sentences.zh: 立其妻劉氏為皇后，太子弘為皇太子。

translations.literal: He established his wife Lady Liu as empress and Crown Prince Hong as imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: He made Lady Liu empress and Crown Prince Hong heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 弘好屬文，親敬儒素。

translations.literal: Hong delighted in literary composition and personally honored scholars of plain virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Hong loved literary composition and personally honored plain scholarly virtue.

sentences.zh: 勒謂徐光曰：「大雅愔愔，殊不似將家子。

translations.literal: Le said to Xu Guang: "Daye is gentle and quiet—quite unlike the son of a general's family.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le said to Xu Guang: "Daye is gentle and quiet—nothing like a general's son.

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「漢祖以馬上取天下，孝文以玄默守之。

translations.literal: " Guang said: "The Han founder took the realm on horseback; Emperor Xiaowen guarded it in silent mysticism.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Guang replied: "The Han founder won the realm on horseback; Emperor Wen kept it through quiet restraint.

sentences.zh: 聖人之後，必有勝殘去殺者，天之道也。

translations.literal: After a sage, there must be one who overcomes cruelty and removes killing—such is Heaven's way.
translations.idiomatic: After a sage always comes one who curbs cruelty and ends killing—that is Heaven's way.

sentences.zh: 」勒甚悅。

translations.literal: " Le was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi Le was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 光因說曰：「皇太子仁孝溫恭，中山王雄暴多詐，陛下一旦不諱，臣恐社稷非太子所有也。

translations.literal: Guang thereupon urged, saying: "The crown prince is benevolent, filial, gentle, and respectful; the King of Zhongshan is fierce, violent, and full of deceit. If Your Majesty should one day pass away unexpectedly, your servant fears the altars of soil and grain will not belong to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang then urged: "The crown prince is benevolent, filial, and mild; the King of Zhongshan is fierce and treacherous. When Your Majesty passes away, I fear the realm will not remain the crown prince's.

sentences.zh: 宜漸奪中山王權，使太子早參朝政。

translations.literal: We ought gradually to strip the King of Zhongshan of power and have the crown prince take part in court affairs early.
translations.idiomatic: You should gradually strip the King of Zhongshan of power and let the crown prince take part in government early.

sentences.zh: 」勒心然之，而未能從。

translations.literal: " Le inwardly agreed but was unable to follow it.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi Le agreed in his heart but could not bring himself to act.

sentences.zh: 趙荊州監軍郭敬寇襄陽。

translations.literal: Later Zhao's military supervisor of Jing Province Guo Jing raided Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao Jing Province military supervisor Guo Jing raided Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 南中郎將周撫監沔北軍事，屯襄陽。

translations.literal: General of the Southern Gentlemen Zhou Fu supervised military affairs north of the Mian River and encamped at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Southern Gentlemen Zhou Fu oversaw military affairs north of the Han and was stationed at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 趙主勒以驛書敕敬退屯樊城，使之偃藏旗幟，寂若無人，曰：「彼若使人觀察，則告之曰：『汝宜自愛堅守，後七八日，大騎將至，相策，不復得走矣。

translations.literal: Zhao ruler Le sent a dispatch by post horse ordering Jing to withdraw and encamp at Fancheng, making him lower and hide banners and flags, silent as if no one were there, saying: "If they send men to observe, then tell them: 'You ought to take care and hold fast—after seven or eight days great cavalry will arrive; when you measure yourselves against them, you will no longer be able to flee.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhao ruler Shi Le dispatched orders by post horse telling Guo Jing to withdraw to Fancheng, hide his banners, and act as if deserted, saying: "If they send scouts, tell them: 'Hold fast and take care—in seven or eight days a great cavalry force will arrive, and you will not be able to escape.'

sentences.zh: 』」敬使人浴馬於津，週而復始，晝夜不絕。

translations.literal: " " Jing had men wash horses at the ford, going round and starting again, without cease day and night.
translations.idiomatic: " " Guo Jing had men watering horses at the ford in an endless cycle, day and night.

sentences.zh: 偵者還以告周撫，撫以為趙兵大至，懼，奔武昌。

translations.literal: The scouts returned and reported to Zhou Fu; Fu thought Zhao's army had arrived in force, grew afraid, and fled to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported back to Zhou Fu, who believed a great Zhao army was coming, panicked, and fled to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 敬入襄陽，中州流民悉降於趙；

translations.literal: Jing entered Xiangyang and all the displaced persons of the central provinces submitted to Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing entered Xiangyang, and refugees from the central provinces all submitted to Zhao;

sentences.zh: 魏該弟遐帥其部眾自石城降敬。

translations.literal: Wei Gai's younger brother Xia led his following from Shicheng to surrender to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gai's brother Xia led his followers from Shicheng to surrender to Guo Jing.

sentences.zh: 敬毀襄陽城，遷其民於沔北，城樊城以戍之。

translations.literal: Jing destroyed the city of Xiangyang, moved its people north of the Mian River, and built up Fancheng to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing razed Xiangyang, relocated its people north of the Han, and fortified Fancheng as a garrison.

sentences.zh: 趙以敬為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhao made Jing Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao appointed Guo Jing governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 周撫坐免官。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 休屠王羌叛趙，趙河東王生擊破之，羌奔涼州。

translations.literal: Xiongnu king of Xiutu Qiang rebelled against Zhao; Zhao's King of Hedong Sheng struck and defeated him, and Qiang fled to Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiutu king Qiang rebelled against Zhao; Hedong King Shi Sheng defeated him, and Qiang fled to Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 西平公駿懼，遣孟毅還，使其長史馬詵稱臣入貢於趙。

translations.literal: Duke of Xiping Jun grew afraid, sent Meng Yi back, and had his Chief Clerk Ma Shen submit tribute to Zhao declaring himself a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Xiping Zhang Jun, alarmed, sent Meng Yi back and had his chief clerk Ma Shen submit tribute to Zhao as a vassal.

sentences.zh: 更造新宮。

translations.literal: A new palace was again constructed.
translations.idiomatic: A new palace was built.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，徙樂成王欽為河間王，封彭城王紘子浚為高密王。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the King of Lecheng Qin was moved to be King of Hejian, and the son Jun of King of Pengcheng Hong was enfeoffed as King of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, King of Lecheng Qin was moved to Hejian, and King of Pengcheng Hong's son Jun was enfeoffed as King of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，成大將軍壽督征南將軍費黑等攻巴東建平，拔之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Great General Shou supervised General Who Conquers the South Fei Hei and others in attacking Jianping in Badong and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Great General Shou led General Who Conquers the South Fei Hei and others against Jianping in Badong and took it.

sentences.zh: 巴東太守楊謙、監軍毌丘奧退保宜都。

translations.literal: Administrator of Badong Yang Qian and military supervisor Guanqiu Ao withdrew to defend Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Badong administrator Yang Qian and military supervisor Guanqiu Ao withdrew to Yidu.

sentences.zh: 顯宗成皇帝上之下咸和六年（

translations.literal: Lower fascicle of the reign of Emperor Cheng the Manifest Ancestor, Xianhe year 6 (
translations.idiomatic: From the lower fascicle of the reign of Emperor Cheng (Manifest Ancestor), Xianhe year 6 (

sentences.zh: 辛卯，公元三三一年）

translations.literal: xinmao, corresponding to 331 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinmao, corresponding to 331 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，趙劉征復寇婁縣，掠武進，郗鑒擊卻之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Liu Zheng of Zhao again raided Lou County, plundered Wujin, and Xi Jian repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Later Zhao's Liu Zheng again raided Lou County and plundered Wujin; Xi Jian drove him back.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day of the month (renxu), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renxu the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 夏，趙主勒如鄴，將營新宮；

translations.literal: In summer, Zhao ruler Le went to Ye and was about to build a new palace;
translations.idiomatic: In summer Zhao ruler Shi Le went to Ye to build a new palace;

sentences.zh: 廷尉上黨續咸苦諫，勒怒，欲斬之。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice Shangdang Xu Xian remonstrated bitterly; Le grew angry and wished to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Justice Xu Xian of Shangdang remonstrated fiercely; Shi Le grew angry and wanted to execute him.

sentences.zh: 中書令徐光曰：「咸言不可用，亦當容之，奈何一旦以直言斬列卿乎！

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Xu Guang said: "Even if Xian's words cannot be used, he ought still to be tolerated—how can you at once execute a ranked minister for blunt speech!
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Xu Guang said: "Even if you cannot use what Xu Xian says, you should still tolerate him—how can you execute a senior minister for speaking plainly!

sentences.zh: 」勒歎曰：「為人君，不得自專如是乎！

translations.literal: " Le sighed and said: "As a ruler of men, can one not even decide for oneself like this!
translations.idiomatic: " Shi Le sighed: "Can a ruler not even decide such things for himself!

sentences.zh: 匹夫家貲滿百匹，猶欲市宅，況富有四海乎！

translations.literal: When a common man's household goods reach a hundred bolts, he still wishes to buy a house—how much more when one possesses all within the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: A commoner with a hundred bolts of silk still wants to buy a house—how much more one who owns the realm!

sentences.zh: 此宮終當營之，且敕停作，以成吾直臣之氣。

translations.literal: This palace will ultimately be built; for now I order construction halted, to complete the spirit of my blunt ministers.
translations.idiomatic: This palace will be built in the end; for now I order work halted to honor my blunt-speaking ministers.

sentences.zh: 」因賜咸絹百匹，稻百斛。

translations.literal: " He thereupon bestowed on Xian a hundred bolts of silk and a hundred hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: " He awarded Xu Xian a hundred bolts of silk and a hundred hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 又詔公卿以下歲舉賢良方正，仍令舉人得更相薦引，以廣求賢之路。

translations.literal: He also decreed that officials from dukes and ministers downward should each year recommend worthy and upright men, and further ordered that those recommended might in turn recommend others, to broaden the paths of seeking the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He also decreed that officials should annually recommend worthy and upright men, and that nominees might recommend others in turn, widening the path for seeking talent.

sentences.zh: 起明堂、辟雍、靈台於襄國城西。

translations.literal: He raised the Bright Hall, Imperial Academy, and Spirit Terrace west of the city of Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Bright Hall, Imperial Academy, and Spirit Terrace west of Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，成大將軍壽攻陰平、武都，楊難敵降之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Great General Shou attacked Yinping and Wudu, and Yang Nan Di surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Great General Shou attacked Yinping and Wudu, and Yang Nan Di submitted.

sentences.zh: 九月，趙主勒復營鄴宮，以洛陽為南都，置行台。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Zhao ruler Le again built the palace at Ye, made Luoyang the Southern Capital, and established a mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Shi Le resumed building at Ye, made Luoyang the southern capital, and established a regional headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 冬，蒸祭太廟，詔歸胙於司徒導，且命無下拜；

translations.literal: In winter, at the winter sacrificial rites to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, an edict returned the sacrificial meat to Director of Works Dao and also ordered that he need not bow down;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, at the winter temple sacrifice, an edict sent sacrificial meat to Minister of Works Wang Dao and exempted him from kneeling;

sentences.zh: 導辭疾不敢當。

translations.literal: Dao declined on grounds of illness and did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 初，帝即位沖幼，每見導必拜，與導手詔則云「惶恐言」，中書作詔則曰「敬問」。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor took the throne he was young, and whenever he saw Dao he would always bow; when he wrote an edict to Dao by his own hand he would say "I speak in trepidation," and when the Secretariat drafted an edict it would say "Respectful inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor acceded to the throne he was very young; whenever he saw Wang Dao he bowed. Personal edicts to Dao began "I speak in trepidation"; Secretariat drafts read "Respectful inquiry."

sentences.zh: 有司議：「元會日，帝應敬導不？

translations.literal: The responsible officials debated: "On New Year's Day assembly, ought the Emperor to show respect to Dao or not?
translations.idiomatic: Officials debated: "On New Year's Day, should the emperor show Wang Dao formal respect?

sentences.zh: 」博士郭熙、杜援議，以為：「禮無拜臣之文，謂宜除敬。

translations.literal: " Erudites Guo Xi and Du Yuan debated, holding: "The rites contain no text on bowing to a minister—we say respect should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: " Erudites Guo Xi and Du Yuan argued that the rites contained no precedent for an emperor bowing to a minister and that formal respect should be dropped.

sentences.zh: 」侍中馮懷議，以為：「天子臨辟雍，拜三老，況先帝師傅！

translations.literal: " Palace Attendant Feng Huai debated, holding: "When the Son of Heaven attends the Imperial Academy he bows to the Three Elders—how much more to the former emperor's teacher!
translations.idiomatic: " Palace Attendant Feng Huai argued that when the Son of Heaven visited the Imperial Academy he bowed to the Three Elders, and Wang Dao had been the former emperor's tutor.

sentences.zh: 謂宜盡敬。

translations.literal: We say full respect should be shown.
translations.idiomatic: Full respect was appropriate.

sentences.zh: 」侍中荀弈議，以為：「三朝之首，宜明君臣之體，則不應敬。

translations.literal: " Palace Attendant Xun Yi debated, holding: "As the foremost of the Three Assemblies, one ought to clarify the form of ruler and minister—therefore one should not show respect.
translations.idiomatic: " Palace Attendant Xun Yi argued that New Year's Day should clarify the ruler-minister relationship, so formal respect was inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 若他日小會，自可盡禮。

translations.literal: If on other days at lesser assemblies, one may naturally observe full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On lesser occasions, full ceremony would still be fitting.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict followed Xun Yi's view.

sentences.zh: 弈，組之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Zu.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi was the son of Xun Zu.

sentences.zh: 慕容廆遣使與太尉陶侃箋，勸以興兵北伐，共清中原。

translations.literal: Murong Hui sent envoys with a letter to Grand Commandant Tao Kan, urging him to raise troops for a northern campaign and together restore the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui sent envoys with a letter to Grand Commandant Tao Kan, urging him to march north and together recover the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 僚屬宋該等共議，以「廆立功一隅，位卑任重，等差無別，不足以鎮華、夷，宜表請進廆官爵。

translations.literal: His staff members Song Gai and others jointly discussed, saying, "Hui has achieved merit in one corner yet holds low rank with heavy responsibility, without clear gradation of honor—this is insufficient to command Chinese and barbarians alike; we ought to memorialize requesting advancement of Hui's office and enfeoffment."
translations.idiomatic: His aides Song Gai and others argued that Hui had won merit on the frontier while holding rank too low for his burden, without the honors needed to command both Chinese and barbarian followers, and that they should petition to advance his titles.

sentences.zh: 」參軍韓恆駁曰：「夫立功者患信義不著，不患名位不高。

translations.literal: " Staff officer Han Heng rebutted: "One who achieves merit should worry that trust and righteousness are not manifest, not that name and rank are not high."
translations.idiomatic: " Staff officer Han Heng objected: "The man who wins merit should fear that his faith and righteousness are not seen, not that his rank is too low."

sentences.zh: 桓、文有匡復之功，不先求禮命以令諸侯。

translations.literal: Dukes Huan and Wen had the achievement of restoring the realm, yet they did not first seek ritual investiture to command the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes Huan and Wen restored the realm, yet they did not first seek formal appointment before rallying the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 宜繕甲兵，除群凶，功成之後，九錫自至。

translations.literal: We should repair armor and weapons, eliminate the mass of villains, and after merit is achieved the Nine Bestowals will come of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: We should sharpen arms, destroy the rebels, and after victory the Nine Bestowals will come in their own time.

sentences.zh: 比於邀君以求寵，不亦榮乎！

translations.literal: Compared with begging the ruler for favor, is this not more glorious!"
translations.idiomatic: Is that not more honorable than begging the throne for rewards?"

sentences.zh: 」廆不悅，出恆為新昌令。

translations.literal: " Hui was displeased and sent Heng out to be magistrate of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui took offense and posted Heng to be magistrate of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 於是東夷校尉封抽等疏上侃府，請封廆為燕王，行大將軍事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Eastern Yi Commandant Feng Chou and others submitted a memorial to Kan's headquarters requesting that Hui be enfeoffed as King of Yan and act as Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Then Eastern Yi Commandant Feng Chou and others memorialized Kan's headquarters to enfeoff Hui as King of Yan with authority as Grand General.

sentences.zh: 侃復書曰：「夫功成進爵，古之成制也。

translations.literal: Kan replied in a letter: "Advancement of rank after achievement of merit is an ancient established rule.
translations.idiomatic: Kan wrote back: "Promotion after merit is the ancient rule.

sentences.zh: 車騎雖未能為官摧勒，然忠義竭誠；

translations.literal: Though the General of Chariots and Cavalry cannot yet drive the official chariot for the court, his loyalty and righteousness are utterly sincere;
translations.idiomatic: Though the General of Chariots and Cavalry has not yet won the court's full commission, his loyalty is beyond question;

sentences.zh: 今騰箋上聽，可不、遲速，當在天台也。

translations.literal: your memorial is now before the throne for hearing; whether it is approved or not, and whether soon or late, rests with the imperial court."
translations.idiomatic: your petition is now before the throne; approval and timing rest with the Son of Heaven."
